## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

# Long Term Vision + Goal

This project explores the most efficient ways to run a variety of AI/LLM generations on **Vulkan** using the AMD AI MAX+ 395 "Strix Halo" platform, with gfx1151 and RDNA3.5. 

Ultimately we want to be able to run these tasks:
  1. Speech to Text via Nvidia's `parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3`:
    * https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2509.14128v2
  2. Text generation via Qwen's `Qwen3.8-Next-Flash`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2608.30320v1
    * We'll need to quantise the weights once we've determined the most efficient method for the hardware
  3. Text to Speech via Hexgrad's `kokoro-82M`:
    * https://huggingface.co/hexgrad/Kokoro-82M
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2306.07691v2
  4. Image generation and editing via Qwen's `Qwen-Image-2.1`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
    * https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1
    * Unified text-to-image and reference-image editing (up to 10 refs), native RGBA transparency
    * In-progress previews: no tiny autoencoder exists yet for its 64-channel VAE,
      so we fit our own linear preview and watch https://github.com/madebyollin/taehv
      for a proper one (replaced z-image-turbo + taef1 on 2026-09-20; plan in IMAGE.md)
  5. Compute embeddings via Qwen's `Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`:
    * https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    * https://arxiv.org/html/2506.05176v3

We will ultimately serve up a HTTP API serving these features, in Go.

1	# IMAGE — the Qwen-Image-2.1 vertical
2	
3	> **Rewritten through 2026-09-20 — one day in, Q0–Q5 are done for t2i** (Q5's
4	> GPU stage excepted) and the model runs end to end in Go: on the CPU it
5	> reproduces diffusers' image to under a quarter of an 8-bit quantization
6	> step, and the **DiT runs on the device at 2.27 s a step — a 1024²/40-step
7	> image's transformer in 90.7 s**. This file is live again: the old root
8	> `IMAGE.md` was frozen into
9	> [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md) at the 2026-09-20
10	> consolidation, and this one is the **replacement of Z-Image-Turbo by
11	> `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`** for both generation and edits. Same rules as every
12	> vertical file: rewritten each session, not appended to; closed stages go to
13	> `research/`. Stage letters here are **Q0, Q1, …** (I-stages stay z-image's,
14	> in the archive).
15	>
16	> Breaking the current vertical while we do this was accepted up front
17	> (2026-09-20 session). Z-Image code gets deleted, not kept in parallel —
18	> except `zimage/qwen`, which `embed`, `llm` and `parakeet` also import
19	> (see "what survives").
20	
21	**Target**: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` — prompt → PNG (optionally RGBA) at up to
22	2048x2048, and native reference-image editing (up to 10 refs), end to end in
23	Go on Vulkan, served at `POST /v1/images/generations` and
24	`POST /v1/images/edits`, with in-progress previews.
25	
26	## Where the work stands
27	
28	| # | Stage | State |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| Q0 | Reference env + dumps (six oracles, `reference/dump_qi21_*.py`) | **done 2026-09-20** — incl. the saved 1024²/40 fp32 run; two runs byte-identical |
31	| Q1 | Text encoding in Go (`qimage/textenc` over an unchanged `zimage/qwen`) | **done** — CPU ≤7.1e-4 (its own noise floor measured), GPU fp16 characterized 10-85x tighter than the official bf16 |
32	| Q2 | One DiT block on CPU (`qimage/dit`) | **done** — block, cache contents, both regimes ≤4e-5; negative control 1e5x |
33	| Q3 | Stack + scheduler + sampler on CPU (`qimage/pipeline`) | **done** — per-step latents 2.1e-5→2.5e-4 vs the oracle |
34	| Q5 | VAE on CPU (`qimage/vae`) + the end-to-end image gate | **done** — decoder/encoder stagewise; **prompt→image matches diffusers at max abs 9.1e-4** (24x inside the 2.2e-2 precedent) |
35	| Q4 | DiT on the GPU (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`) | **done for t2i** — teacher-forced flat ≤8e-3 over 40 steps; **2.27 s/step at 1024²** |
36	| Q5g | VAE on the GPU | **open — the serving blocker**: the CPU decoder's ~20 s at 256² extrapolates to minutes at 1024², dwarfing the 91 s DiT |
37	| Q6 | Serve t2i (`/v1/images/generations`, RGBA, ceiling geometry) | open — plus the step-count sweep that sets the default |
38	| Q7 | Previews (fitted linear 64→RGB; no tiny AE exists for this VAE) | open |
39	| Q8 | Edits (vision tower, multi-ref, VAE encoder serving) | open — the largest remaining port |
40	| Q9 | Percents (fusion ports, tile re-screens, the full-seq re-pack) | open, deliberately last |
41	
42	Every gate is dump-driven and every tolerance in this file is measured, with
43	the instrument named beside it. The day's method finding, twice over: when a
44	port exceeds a borrowed tolerance, measure the *reference against itself*
45	(swap its attention kernel, its thread count, its dtype) before hunting a
46	bug — three of the bounds below are set that way.
47	
48	**References, in the order to reach for them:**
49	
50	- `models/Qwen-Image-2.1/` — the checkpoint is cloned; configs quoted below
51	  are read from it, not from docs.
52	- `reference/qwenimage21/{pipeline,transformer,autoencoder_kl}_qwenimage21.py`
53	  — the **merged** diffusers implementation (PR
54	  [huggingface/diffusers#14804](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14804)),
55	  copied verbatim 2026-09-20. This is the oracle every dump comes from.
56	- [Model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) ·
57	  [blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1) (JS-only page, fetch fails —
58	  the model card and PR carry the same facts) ·
59	  [examples repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) ·
60	  [sglang port](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39983) (a second
61	  implementation to cross-check against; its follow-ups
62	  [#40447](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40447) document the
63	  per-layer prefix-cache layout).
64	- License: **Qwen Research License** (`models/Qwen-Image-2.1/LICENSE`) — not
65	  Apache like Z-Image was. Fine for this project; worth remembering if the
66	  server ever grows other users.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## The model, as the checkpoint describes it
71	
72	Three components, ~32.3 GB on disk (bf16), against Z-Image's ~20 GB resident:
73	
74	| | | |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| DiT | `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` — **32 single-stream blocks**, dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), SwiGLU **12288** (mlp_ratio 3), **no biases anywhere**, per-head-dim q/k RMSNorm (eps 1e-6), 7.1 B params | 14 GB |
77	| Text encoder | **Qwen3-VL-8B** (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`): text model 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 q / 8 kv heads of 128, theta **5e6**, vocab 151936; plus a 27-layer vision tower (hidden 1152, patch 16, spatial-merge 2, deepstack taps at layers 8/16/24) | 17 GB |
78	| VAE | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` — Wan-lineage causal-3D residual conv AE, encoder base 96 / decoder base **144**, dim_mult [1,2,4,8,8], **z_dim 64, 16x spatial**, **4-channel RGBA in and out**, per-channel `latents_mean/std` (64 values each) | 1.3 GB |
79	
80	Geometry: **one latent token = one 16x16 pixel tile** (patch_size 1, VAE /16).
81	Pixel sides must be multiples of **32** (the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2).
82	1024² = 4096 image tokens — the same DiT sequence length as Z-Image at 1024².
83	2048² (the model's native size) = 16384. Defaults: **40 steps, no CFG**
84	(`true_cfg_scale=1.0`; true-CFG exists but is off by design), pipeline default
85	resolution **1024²** (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly).
86	
87	### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image
88	
89	**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
90	share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
91	the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
92	condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
93	non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
94	segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
95	the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.
96	
97	**2. `causal_condition` + prefix KV cache.** Text and condition-image tokens
98	are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
99	target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
100	That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
101	full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
102	steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
103	[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
104	padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
105	for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
106	on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
107	settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
108	cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**
109	
110	**3. Sequence assembly and RoPE.** The VLM sequence's `<|image_pad|>` slots
111	each stand for a **2x2 group of latent tokens**: the transformer expands those
112	positions four-fold and drops VAE latents into them; the target's slots are
113	appended after the text. Text embeddings pass through `txt_in` (zero-centered
114	RMSNorm → 4096→4096 → GELU-tanh → 4096→4096); latents through `img_in`
115	(64→4096, no bias). RoPE is 3-axis (frame/h/w, dims 16/56/56, theta 10000),
116	complex adjacent-pair rotation — **the same pairing as Z-Image's DiT**, not
117	the NeoX halves of the text encoder. Text advances all three axes together;
118	each image block freezes the frame axis and lays h/w out on a **zero-centered
119	grid with negative indices** (a flipped negative-frequency table serves
120	indices −1024..−1); after an image block the position cursor advances by
121	`max(h, w)`.
122	
123	**4. Shared modulation.** One `SiLU → Linear(4096→16384)` for the whole
124	model — blocks own no adaLN parameters. Each block chunks it into
125	(scale1, gate1, scale2, gate2); gates pass through **tanh**; norms are plain
126	non-affine LayerNorm. Final head: scale-only AdaLN + `proj_out` 4096→64.
127	Timestep embedding: sinusoidal 256 (cos first half — Z-Image convention
128	differs, check the dump), then a bias-free MLP to 4096.
129	
130	### Text encoding, exactly
131	
132	Raw template strings, **not** `apply_chat_template` (the two tokenize
133	differently and the checkpoint expects the raw form):
134	
135	```
136	t2i:  <|im_start|>system\nComprehend and analyze the provided prompt.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n{prompt}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n
137	edit: same, with "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" (then " <image2>…" etc.) prefixed to the user text
138	```
139	
140	- The embedding is the **last decoder layer's output *before* the final
141	  RMSNorm** (all 36 layers run — different from Z-Image's `hidden_states[-2]`
142	  where the last layer never ran). transformers 5.x silently normalizes
143	  `hidden_states[-1]`; diffusers neutralizes that with a forward hook on the
144	  final norm, and Q0 **verified the hook on transformers 5.17.0**: the hooked
145	  `hidden_states[-1]` equals the pipeline's output exactly (gap 0), so 5.17
146	  is the dump env — the model card requires >= 5.17 anyway.
147	- Drop the first `drop_idx` tokens, where drop_idx = length of the tokenized
148	  system message (computed, not hardcoded). Empty prompt becomes `" "`.
149	- For edits, condition images additionally go through the vision tower (RGBA
150	  flattened over white **for the vision copy only**); mrope with real 3D
151	  positions at image slots. Text-only prompts make mrope collapse to standard
152	  NeoX RoPE — **verified in Q0**: the model's own cos/sin tables for a text
153	  prompt match a plain theta-5e6 table to 0.0 (`mrope_gap` in the textenc
154	  manifest), so nothing mrope-shaped is needed before Q8.
155	- A fact Q8 rests on, confirmed while building the head dump: **the VLM's
156	  image-slot embedding rows are overwritten by the VAE latents** in the joint
157	  stream. Vision content reaches the DiT only through what the *text* tokens
158	  absorbed from the image inside the text encoder's own attention. The vision
159	  tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels.
160	
161	### Scheduler
162	
163	FlowMatchEulerDiscrete with **dynamic shifting**: sigmas `linspace(1, 1/N, N)`,
164	`mu` linear in the **target** token count between (256, 0.5) and (8192, 0.9)
165	— at 1024², mu = 0.6935, and **unclamped past 8192**: 2048² extrapolates to
166	mu = 1.3129 (measured, Q0) — `time_shift_type: exponential`,
167	`shift_terminal: 0.02`, `stochastic_sampling: false`. Port from diffusers'
168	scheduler, not from Z-Image's fixed shift 3.0. The scheduler steps **only the
169	target latents** (the model's output rows for the prefix are discarded).
170	VAE decode applies `z * std + mean` per channel; encode the inverse, and uses
171	the **posterior mode** (`argmax`), which keeps our seed-reproducibility rule
172	for free.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## What this changes about the vertical (semantics, not code)
177	
178	- **Edits stop being SDEdit.** Today an edit is a truncated generation
179	  (strength ⇒ steps skipped ⇒ cheaper). In 2.1 an edit is a *conditional
180	  generation*: reference latents + vision context as prefix, target from pure
181	  noise, all 40 steps. An edit becomes **slightly more expensive** than a
182	  generation (bigger prefix), the `strength` knob disappears, and up to **10
183	  reference images** arrive (OpenAI's `image[]` array already allows several).
184	  `/v1/images/edits` keeps its shape; its documentation changes meaning.
185	- **RGBA is native.** The VAE emits 4 channels always; transparency is asked
186	  for in the prompt (the model card's recommended phrasing). Map OpenAI's
187	  `background: "transparent"` to that prompt prefix + PNG-with-alpha out;
188	  opaque requests composite over white.
189	- **Masked / annotated local edits** (circles, painted regions, separate
190	  masks) are a *capability the model has* — the current 501 for masks may
191	  become closable. How a separate mask is fed (extra condition image?) is not
192	  in the diffusers PR; needs the examples repo before promising it (open
193	  question Q-o3).
194	- **The cost profile inverts — now measured, no longer estimated.**
195	  Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation at 14.3 s an image; 2.1 wants 40
196	  steps, and Q4's GPU DiT measures **2.27 s a cached step, 2.29 s the
197	  prefill: 90.7 s of transformer per 1024² image** (the morning's estimate
198	  said ~70 s; the gap is unported fusions and the full-seq re-pack, priced
199	  under Q9). What a *served* image costs also needs the VAE's GPU stage
200	  (Q5g — the CPU decoder would add minutes) and the text encoder's ~1 s.
201	  2048² is still an estimate: GEMMs x4 and attention x16 over the 91 s.
202	  The two levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for
203	  quality — the knob exists, and at 2.27 s/step it is the difference between
204	  ~90 s and ~27 s) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
205	  — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch for it).
206	  **Q6's sweep decides the served default**; 1024²/40 is the starting point,
207	  not a commitment.
208	
209	## The preview problem (taef1 has no successor here)
210	
211	`madebyollin/taehv`'s **taew2_1 does *not* fit this model**: it decodes the
212	Wan-2.1 16-channel/8x latent that the *original* Qwen-Image borrowed; 2.1's
213	VAE is a new 64-channel/16x RGBA design, and as of today taehv lists nothing
214	for it. So, in order:
215	
216	1. **Q7 ships a fitted linear preview**: a 64→3 (or →4) matrix, least-squares
217	   over dumped (latent, 1/16-scale image) pairs — the latent2rgb approach.
218	   One GEMV per pixel, effectively free per step; a 1024² generation previews
219	   at 64x64, upscaled client-side. Fitting data comes out of Q0's dumps.
220	2. **Watch taehv** for a 2.1 variant and port it like `zimage/vae/tiny.go`
221	   (at T=1 its temporal machinery degenerates; it would be a small 2D conv
222	   stack again). Do not build our own distilled decoder — that is a training
223	   project this repo does not want.
224	
225	## What survives, what is new, what dies
226	
227	| piece | verdict |
228	|---|---|
229	| `zimage/qwen` (Qwen3 text transformer, CPU + GPU) | **survives and grows** — it is shared infra (`embed`, `llm`, `parakeet` import it). Q1 adds: theta as config (5e6), 36-layer/pre-final-norm output mode beside the existing `EncoderLayers()` convention, and (Q8 only) mrope + deepstack + the vision tower. The Qwen3-Embedding caller must keep passing its tests untouched. |
230	| `zimage/tokenizer` | **survives** — same BPE family; new `added_tokens.json` (`<image1>`…, vision markers) and the raw template above. |
231	| shaders: `dit_gemm_*`, `dit_attention_*` (WMMA), gpu arenas | **survived, confirmed by Q4** — the whole graph runs on z-image's kernels plus two new small shaders (`dit_attn_causal`, `dit_copy`). The new shapes run on z-image's measured winners *uncontested*: the tile re-screen at M=16384/K=12288 is a Q9 percent (hypothesis 5 in `TODO.md`). |
232	| `zimage/vae/gpu_conv*` | **survives as infrastructure** — the conv/groupnorm kernels feed the new VAE port. |
233	| `zimage/dit`, `zimage/vae` (model code), `zimage/pipeline` | **die** — replaced by a new `qimage/` tree (`qimage/dit`, `qimage/vae`, `qimage/pipeline`). New names because almost no line survives: different block, different mask, different VAE family. Delete z-image code as each Q-stage lands its replacement, not in one purge. |
234	| `cmd/zimage`, `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/vaebench`, … | retargeted to `qimage` equivalents as their stage arrives. |
235	| `models/Z-Image-Turbo`, `models/taef1` (62 GB) | delete from disk once Q6 serves — not before, so A/B stays possible. |
236	| serving: `/v1/images/*`, streaming, geometry-under-a-ceiling | **survives in shape** — I1/I2's design carries over; the adapter re-wires to `qimage/pipeline`. |
237	
238	Two-machine deployment holds: image goes ~26 → **~36–40 GB resident**
239	(weights 32.3 GB fp16 + activations), sharing a 128 GB box with speech + TTS +
240	embeddings (~3 GB). Still no footprint quantisation.
241	
242	## The stages
243	
244	Same doctrine as every vertical: **CPU reference first, validated against a
245	dump, then the GPU port debugged against the CPU one.** One stage, one gate,
246	two-run numbers.
247	
248	- **Q0 — reference environment and dumps. Done 2026-09-20**, full-size
249	  oracle included: `out/qi21run1024` is the saved 1024²/40 fp32 CPU run
250	  (~52 s/step, ~35 min, ~68 GB — nothing else heavy may run beside it; a
251	  34 GB Go test alongside got both OOM-killed), and its PNG is a
252	  photorealistic render of the prompt. The env: the shared `.venv` with torch
253	  2.14.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, torchvision 0.29.0+cpu, accelerate, and
254	  **diffusers 0.41.0.dev0 pinned to git commit `80c7ed26`** (stable 0.40.0
255	  predates the merge); `reference/qwenimage21/` is byte-identical to the
256	  installed package. Five scripts, all fp32 CPU, all in `reference/`:
257	  - `dump_qi21_sched.py` → `out/qi21sched` — sigma/timestep tables for five
258	    size/step cases plus one Euler step over deterministic vectors.
259	  - `dump_qi21_dit.py` → `out/qi21dit` — everything around the blocks
260	    (num_layers=0, 9 tensors): txt_in/img_in, joint assembly, RoPE tables,
261	    image_ids/target mask, the t=0 modulation row, prefill and cached
262	    forwards, for a t2i case and a synthetic edit case. The
263	    prefill-vs-cached identity at 0 blocks measured exactly 0.
264	  - `dump_qi21_dit_block.py` → `out/qi21block` — block 0 with real weights
265	    in prefill/extract/cached modes, cache K/V contents included; the fp32
266	    cached-vs-prefill gap on target rows measured **≤ 3.8e-6** (t2i), 0
267	    (edit) — Q4's numeric bound.
268	  - `dump_qi21_vae.py` → `out/qi21vae` — decode from seeded noise and encode
269	    of a deterministic RGBA test card (posterior **mode**), per-child and
270	    per-up/down-block intermediates hooked, 256² and 192x320. Decode clamps
271	    to [-1,1]; encoder conv_out is 128 = 64 mean + 64 logvar.
272	  - `dump_qi21_run.py` → `out/qi21run` + `out/qi21run2` — the end-to-end
273	    oracle: 256²/4 steps, seed 42, kv-cache on, noise passed in packed (the
274	    Go side gets it as data, not torch RNG), per-step latents, final RGBA
275	    image + PNG. **Two runs byte-identical**, and the PNG is recognizably
276	    the prompt. `--size 1024 --steps 40 --out out/qi21run1024` is the saved
277	    full-size run.
278	  - `dump_qi21_textenc.py` → `out/qi21textenc` — runs the pipeline's own
279	    `_get_qwen_prompt_embeds` (en / cjk / empty prompts), plus a layer walk
280	    (embed, layers 0-1, last-prenorm) and the rope cos/sin capture that
281	    settled Q-o5. drop_idx = 14 for the shipped system prompt.
282	- **Q1 — text encoding in Go. Done 2026-09-20.** `zimage/qwen` needed **no
283	  change at all** — `qimage/textenc` (the tree's first package) supplies the
284	  nested-`text_config` adapter (Prefix `model.language_model.`), the raw t2i
285	  template, the tokenized-system-message drop, and `Drop`; `Load(dir,
286	  cfg.NumLayers)` already expresses "all 36 layers, no final norm". Gates:
287	  tokenizer exact on en/cjk/empty; layer walk ≤ 2e-5; **CPU encoder en
288	  1.6e-4 / cjk 8.6e-5 / empty 7.1e-4 against a `deepTol` of 1e-3** — measured,
289	  not chosen: the reference disagrees with *itself* by 3.2e-4 on the empty
290	  prompt when only the attention kernel changes (eager vs sdpa), so
291	  z-image's 2e-4 sits below this model's own fp32 noise floor at depth 36.
292	  **GPU encoder (fp16, unchanged kernels) en/cjk 0.024-0.027, empty 0.21**,
293	  and that number has a mechanism (`TestGPULadder`, kept as the permanent
294	  instrument): the residual stream grows a ~13k massive-activation channel
295	  at layer 6, carries it flat, and **cancels it in layers 34-35 — the two
296	  layers Z-Image never ran** — so the fp16 bulk-rounding variance the
297	  channel accumulated surfaces at the end (protecting just the spike
298	  elements measurably does not help). Priced against deployment: the
299	  **official bf16 pipeline deviates from fp32 by rel 2.0 (abs 204)** through
300	  the same mechanism — our fp16 path is 10-85x closer to fp32 than what the
301	  ecosystem ships. Not taken (priced): an fp32-activation GEMM arm for the
302	  encoder — at prompt-sized M (~40 rows) the encoder is weight-bandwidth-
303	  bound so it would be cheap; build it only if Q3/Q6 show prompt adherence
304	  suffering.
305	- **Q2 — one DiT block on CPU. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/dit`): layout
306	  (image ids/target mask/segments) **exact** vs the dump, RoPE tables at
307	  ~5e-7 (negative-index grids included), head pieces at ~1e-5, the no-block
308	  prefill/cached forwards at ~4e-6, and the block gate — out_prefill,
309	  cache K/V contents, out_cached, both cases — at **≤ 4e-5** against
310	  `out/qi21block`. The negative control (NeoX-halves rotary pairing) is
311	  caught at 1e5x the bound. `Load(dir, blocks)` takes 0/1/32 blocks, so Q3's
312	  stack is a loop away. One porting trap found and worth remembering:
313	  `chunk(2, -1)` splits *rows* — rewrapping the modulation's backing array
314	  at half width hands row 1 the second half of row 0, and every downstream
315	  tensor fails at rel ~10 while every shape checks out.
316	- **Q3 — the stack + scheduler + t2i sampler on CPU. Done 2026-09-20 at the
317	  latent gate** (`qimage/pipeline`): the dynamic-shift scheduler matches
318	  diffusers at ~1e-6 across all five dumped size/step cases (mu exact, the
319	  exponential shift, the terminal stretch, the Euler step), and
320	  `Denoise` — 32 blocks, ModeExtract at step 0 then cached decodes, exactly
321	  as served — reproduces the 256²/4-step oracle's **per-step latents at
322	  rel 2.1e-5 → 2.5e-4** (bound 1e-3, 4x measured; 2.3 min a sample on CPU).
323	  **Still owed to Q5**: the *image* gate — prompt → PNG with our own text
324	  encoder and VAE decode against the oracle's `image` tensor (Z-Image's
325	  2.2e-2 precedent). The three green gates (textenc, denoise, decoder) do
326	  not compose into that claim; it gets measured, once the decoder exists.
327	- **Q4 — DiT on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20 for t2i** (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`,
328	  ~750 lines on z-image's shader set): **1024²/40 steps in 90.7 s — prefill
329	  2.29 s, cached steps 2.27 s** — against CPU Go's ~2.5 h and torch fp32's
330	  ~35 min. The mapping that made it small: the block's LayerNorm+modulate+
331	  narrow is `dit_final_norm.comp` verbatim; the shared modulation is host
332	  arithmetic (ten uploaded vectors) with the t=0 row-select expressed as two
333	  dispatch ranges; SwiGLU's fp16 range problem is solved *exactly* by
334	  scaling 1/16 into fp16 and folding 16 into the uploaded tanh(gate) vector
335	  (2.1's down-proj feeds a gated residual, so z-image's norm-invariance
336	  trick was unavailable). Two new shaders: `dit_attn_causal.comp` (the
337	  prefill runs the WMMA kernel bidirectionally over the whole sequence and
338	  this recomputes the text rows' context causally — tens of rows, once per
339	  image) and `dit_copy.comp` (offset copies for the KV cache). The cache is
340	  each block's post-RoPE prefix k/v as fp32 arena rows, restored under the
341	  fresh target rows each step before a full re-pack (fine at t2i's tiny
342	  prefix; Q8's reference images want it fp16 + tile-masked, and the
343	  full-seq re-pack is a Q9 percent). **Gates, per
344	  `two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate`, both regimes against the oracle**:
345	  teacher-forced (each step fed the oracle's own latents — bounds the
346	  model) flat at 1.5e-3–8e-3 over all 40 steps at 1024², bound 2e-2;
347	  free-running drifts linearly at ~1.3e-3/step to 0.050 at 40 steps — a
348	  perturbed ODE diverging, the phenomenon diffusers documents for
349	  cache-on/off — bounded at 0.12 with the image judgment deferred to Q6's
350	  eyeball. Not done: tile re-screen at M=16384/K=12288 (running on
351	  z-image's measured winners uncontested — a Q9 percent), the VAE's GPU
352	  stage (with Q5's fp16-range constraint), and the negative-control
353	  breakages the z-image graph carries.
354	- **Q5 — the VAE in Go. CPU done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/vae`, on
355	  `zimage/vae`'s Tensor/Conv2D — whose Pad/PadEnd/Stride already carried the
356	  identical downsampler shape): decoder and encoder, stagewise against
357	  `out/qi21vae`, RGBA round trip included. The T=1 semantics are explicit in
358	  the package doc: causal 3D convs fold to 2D, time_convs never run,
359	  AvgDown3D *means in a zero frame* on temporal blocks, DupUp3D keeps only
360	  the last temporal copy. Two measured bounds: conv stages at 2e-4 (they run
361	  at ≤5e-5), and `normTol` 8e-3 for the stages where the model amplifies
362	  fp32 noise — the decoder past its per-pixel L2 tail norm (the dumped fp32
363	  reference is itself rel 1.3e-3 from a float64 decode there; our decoded
364	  image sits max abs 8.7e-4 from the dump, under a quarter of one 8-bit
365	  step) and the encoder's deep middle (the reference's own thread-order
366	  noise jumps 47x at down_blocks.3; we track ~5x that and land at 4.7e-5 on
367	  the posterior mode).
368	  **The end-to-end image gate Q3 owed is closed**: `TestEndToEndImage` runs
369	  prompt → image through our tokenizer, text encoder, DiT, scheduler and
370	  decoder — only the noise is the oracle's — and matches the 256²/4-step
371	  reference image at **max abs 9.1e-4, mean 6e-6** in [0, 1] space, 24x
372	  inside the 2.2e-2 precedent. (~65 GB fp32 passes through, sequenced to a
373	  ~34 GB peak; it must run alone.)
374	  **Still open in Q5: the GPU port**, which folds into Q4's GPU stage — and
375	  the fp16 constraint from Q0 stands: decoder intermediates reach absmax
376	  ~1e5–3e5 against fp16's 65504, so those stages need fp32 storage or a
377	  rescale, unlike z-image's decoder.
378	- **Q6 — serve t2i.** Blocked on **Q5g, the VAE's GPU stage** (the CPU
379	  decoder would add minutes to a 91 s DiT; z-image's `gpu_conv` infra is the
380	  base, and Q0's fp16-range finding applies — decoder intermediates reach
381	  ~3e5, so those stages stay fp32 or rescale). Then: `-image` loads qimage;
382	  `/v1/images/generations` with geometry under a ceiling (multiples of 32
383	  now, not 16), `background: "transparent"`, steps default 40. **First
384	  honest served wall clock** (two runs) at 1024² and 2048², the free-run
385	  image eyeball Q4 deferred here, and the **step-count sweep** (40/24/16/12,
386	  same seed, a fixed prompt set) that decides the served default. Delete
387	  Z-Image weights and dead code after this lands.
388	- **Q7 — previews.** Fit the linear 64→RGB matrix from Q0's pairs, wire
389	  `stream: true`/`partial_images` back up.
390	- **Q8 — edits.** The big one, in three parts: (a) VAE encoder serving
391	  reference latents (Q5 built it), (b) **the vision tower** — 27-layer ViT,
392	  2x2 spatial merge, interpolated position grid, deepstack feature injection
393	  into the text model's first layers, mrope with real 3D positions — the
394	  largest genuinely new port in this migration, (c) multi-image template +
395	  per-ref RoPE blocks + prefix cache across refs. `/v1/images/edits` drops
396	  `strength`, gains multi-ref. Gate: edit dump match + an end-to-end edit vs
397	  the oracle.
398	- **Q9 — percents.** Only after capabilities: the I3/I5/I8/I9 fusion lesson
399	  (elementwise passes absorbed into consumers) transfers to a new but
400	  same-shaped budget; attribute before optimising, same-hour controls, plans
401	  measured never composed.
402	
403	## Decisions taken now (so future sessions don't relitigate)
404	
405	1. **New `qimage/` tree; `zimage/qwen` and `zimage/tokenizer` stay put** until
406	   z-image is fully gone, then a mechanical rename can hoist them.
407	2. **KV cache always on** — validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`;
408	   cache-off exists only as a debug path if Q4 needs it.
409	3. **Posterior mode (argmax) for every VAE encode** — matches the reference
410	   and our reproducibility rule.
411	4. **1024² default, 2048² behind the ceiling flag**, pending Q6's numbers.
412	5. **No self-trained tiny decoder**; linear preview + watch taehv.
413	6. **No CFG path in the Go port** (true_cfg_scale stays a refusal if asked
414	   for over HTTP) until something demands it — it would double every step.
415	
416	## Open questions
417	
418	- **Q-o1**: how far below 40 steps does quality hold? (Q6 sweep; also decides
419	  whether the vertical's headline is ~30 s or ~70 s.)
420	- **Q-o2**: does a turbo/distilled 2.1 checkpoint or step-distillation LoRA
421	  appear? (Watch the examples repo and lightx2v.)
422	- **Q-o3**: how are separate masks / painted annotations fed for local edits?
423	  (Examples repo, before `/v1/images/edits` promises masks.)
424	- **Q-o4**: does taehv grow a 2.1 variant? (Q7 fallback becomes an upgrade.)
425	- ~~**Q-o5**: text-only mrope — confirmed equivalent to plain RoPE by dump?~~
426	  **Settled 2026-09-20 (Q0)**: gap 0.0 against a plain theta-5e6 NeoX table;
427	  `zimage/qwen` needs nothing mrope-shaped before Q8.

# IMAGE — the Qwen-Image-2.1 vertical

> **Rewritten through 2026-09-20 — one day in, Q0–Q5 are done for t2i** (Q5's
> GPU stage excepted) and the model runs end to end in Go: on the CPU it
> reproduces diffusers' image to under a quarter of an 8-bit quantization
> step, and the **DiT runs on the device at 2.27 s a step — a 1024²/40-step
> image's transformer in 90.7 s**. This file is live again: the old root
> `IMAGE.md` was frozen into
> [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md) at the 2026-09-20
> consolidation, and this one is the **replacement of Z-Image-Turbo by
> `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`** for both generation and edits. Same rules as every
> vertical file: rewritten each session, not appended to; closed stages go to
> `research/`. Stage letters here are **Q0, Q1, …** (I-stages stay z-image's,
> in the archive).
>
> Breaking the current vertical while we do this was accepted up front
> (2026-09-20 session). Z-Image code gets deleted, not kept in parallel —
> except `zimage/qwen`, which `embed`, `llm` and `parakeet` also import
> (see "what survives").

**Target**: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` — prompt → PNG (optionally RGBA) at up to
2048x2048, and native reference-image editing (up to 10 refs), end to end in
Go on Vulkan, served at `POST /v1/images/generations` and
`POST /v1/images/edits`, with in-progress previews.

## Where the work stands

| # | Stage | State |
|---|---|---|
| Q0 | Reference env + dumps (six oracles, `reference/dump_qi21_*.py`) | **done 2026-09-20** — incl. the saved 1024²/40 fp32 run; two runs byte-identical |
| Q1 | Text encoding in Go (`qimage/textenc` over an unchanged `zimage/qwen`) | **done** — CPU ≤7.1e-4 (its own noise floor measured), GPU fp16 characterized 10-85x tighter than the official bf16 |
| Q2 | One DiT block on CPU (`qimage/dit`) | **done** — block, cache contents, both regimes ≤4e-5; negative control 1e5x |
| Q3 | Stack + scheduler + sampler on CPU (`qimage/pipeline`) | **done** — per-step latents 2.1e-5→2.5e-4 vs the oracle |
| Q5 | VAE on CPU (`qimage/vae`) + the end-to-end image gate | **done** — decoder/encoder stagewise; **prompt→image matches diffusers at max abs 9.1e-4** (24x inside the 2.2e-2 precedent) |
| Q4 | DiT on the GPU (`qimage/dit/gpu.go`) | **done for t2i** — teacher-forced flat ≤8e-3 over 40 steps; **2.27 s/step at 1024²** |
| Q5g | VAE on the GPU | **open — the serving blocker**: the CPU decoder's ~20 s at 256² extrapolates to minutes at 1024², dwarfing the 91 s DiT |
| Q6 | Serve t2i (`/v1/images/generations`, RGBA, ceiling geometry) | open — plus the step-count sweep that sets the default |
| Q7 | Previews (fitted linear 64→RGB; no tiny AE exists for this VAE) | open |
| Q8 | Edits (vision tower, multi-ref, VAE encoder serving) | open — the largest remaining port |
| Q9 | Percents (fusion ports, tile re-screens, the full-seq re-pack) | open, deliberately last |

Every gate is dump-driven and every tolerance in this file is measured, with
the instrument named beside it. The day's method finding, twice over: when a
port exceeds a borrowed tolerance, measure the *reference against itself*
(swap its attention kernel, its thread count, its dtype) before hunting a
bug — three of the bounds below are set that way.

**References, in the order to reach for them:**

- `models/Qwen-Image-2.1/` — the checkpoint is cloned; configs quoted below
  are read from it, not from docs.
- `reference/qwenimage21/{pipeline,transformer,autoencoder_kl}_qwenimage21.py`
  — the **merged** diffusers implementation (PR
  [huggingface/diffusers#14804](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/pull/14804)),
  copied verbatim 2026-09-20. This is the oracle every dump comes from.
- [Model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1) ·
  [blog](https://qwen.ai/blog?id=qwen-image-2.1) (JS-only page, fetch fails —
  the model card and PR carry the same facts) ·
  [examples repo](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen-Image-2.1) ·
  [sglang port](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39983) (a second
  implementation to cross-check against; its follow-ups
  [#40447](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40447) document the
  per-layer prefix-cache layout).
- License: **Qwen Research License** (`models/Qwen-Image-2.1/LICENSE`) — not
  Apache like Z-Image was. Fine for this project; worth remembering if the
  server ever grows other users.

---

## The model, as the checkpoint describes it

Three components, ~32.3 GB on disk (bf16), against Z-Image's ~20 GB resident:

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| DiT | `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel` — **32 single-stream blocks**, dim 4096 (32 heads x 128), SwiGLU **12288** (mlp_ratio 3), **no biases anywhere**, per-head-dim q/k RMSNorm (eps 1e-6), 7.1 B params | 14 GB |
| Text encoder | **Qwen3-VL-8B** (`Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`): text model 36 layers, hidden 4096, 32 q / 8 kv heads of 128, theta **5e6**, vocab 151936; plus a 27-layer vision tower (hidden 1152, patch 16, spatial-merge 2, deepstack taps at layers 8/16/24) | 17 GB |
| VAE | `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21` — Wan-lineage causal-3D residual conv AE, encoder base 96 / decoder base **144**, dim_mult [1,2,4,8,8], **z_dim 64, 16x spatial**, **4-channel RGBA in and out**, per-channel `latents_mean/std` (64 values each) | 1.3 GB |

Geometry: **one latent token = one 16x16 pixel tile** (patch_size 1, VAE /16).
Pixel sides must be multiples of **32** (the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2).
1024² = 4096 image tokens — the same DiT sequence length as Z-Image at 1024².
2048² (the model's native size) = 16384. Defaults: **40 steps, no CFG**
(`true_cfg_scale=1.0`; true-CFG exists but is off by design), pipeline default
resolution **1024²** (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly).

### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image

**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.

**2. `causal_condition` + prefix KV cache.** Text and condition-image tokens
are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**

**3. Sequence assembly and RoPE.** The VLM sequence's `<|image_pad|>` slots
each stand for a **2x2 group of latent tokens**: the transformer expands those
positions four-fold and drops VAE latents into them; the target's slots are
appended after the text. Text embeddings pass through `txt_in` (zero-centered
RMSNorm → 4096→4096 → GELU-tanh → 4096→4096); latents through `img_in`
(64→4096, no bias). RoPE is 3-axis (frame/h/w, dims 16/56/56, theta 10000),
complex adjacent-pair rotation — **the same pairing as Z-Image's DiT**, not
the NeoX halves of the text encoder. Text advances all three axes together;
each image block freezes the frame axis and lays h/w out on a **zero-centered
grid with negative indices** (a flipped negative-frequency table serves
indices −1024..−1); after an image block the position cursor advances by
`max(h, w)`.

**4. Shared modulation.** One `SiLU → Linear(4096→16384)` for the whole
model — blocks own no adaLN parameters. Each block chunks it into
(scale1, gate1, scale2, gate2); gates pass through **tanh**; norms are plain
non-affine LayerNorm. Final head: scale-only AdaLN + `proj_out` 4096→64.
Timestep embedding: sinusoidal 256 (cos first half — Z-Image convention
differs, check the dump), then a bias-free MLP to 4096.

### Text encoding, exactly

Raw template strings, **not** `apply_chat_template` (the two tokenize
differently and the checkpoint expects the raw form):

```
t2i:  <|im_start|>system\nComprehend and analyze the provided prompt.<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n{prompt}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n
edit: same, with "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>" (then " <image2>…" etc.) prefixed to the user text
```

- The embedding is the **last decoder layer's output *before* the final
  RMSNorm** (all 36 layers run — different from Z-Image's `hidden_states[-2]`
  where the last layer never ran). transformers 5.x silently normalizes
  `hidden_states[-1]`; diffusers neutralizes that with a forward hook on the
  final norm, and Q0 **verified the hook on transformers 5.17.0**: the hooked
  `hidden_states[-1]` equals the pipeline's output exactly (gap 0), so 5.17
  is the dump env — the model card requires >= 5.17 anyway.
- Drop the first `drop_idx` tokens, where drop_idx = length of the tokenized
  system message (computed, not hardcoded). Empty prompt becomes `" "`.
- For edits, condition images additionally go through the vision tower (RGBA
  flattened over white **for the vision copy only**); mrope with real 3D
  positions at image slots. Text-only prompts make mrope collapse to standard
  NeoX RoPE — **verified in Q0**: the model's own cos/sin tables for a text
  prompt match a plain theta-5e6 table to 0.0 (`mrope_gap` in the textenc
  manifest), so nothing mrope-shaped is needed before Q8.
- A fact Q8 rests on, confirmed while building the head dump: **the VLM's
  image-slot embedding rows are overwritten by the VAE latents** in the joint
  stream. Vision content reaches the DiT only through what the *text* tokens
  absorbed from the image inside the text encoder's own attention. The vision
  tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels.

### Scheduler

FlowMatchEulerDiscrete with **dynamic shifting**: sigmas `linspace(1, 1/N, N)`,
`mu` linear in the **target** token count between (256, 0.5) and (8192, 0.9)
— at 1024², mu = 0.6935, and **unclamped past 8192**: 2048² extrapolates to
mu = 1.3129 (measured, Q0) — `time_shift_type: exponential`,
`shift_terminal: 0.02`, `stochastic_sampling: false`. Port from diffusers'
scheduler, not from Z-Image's fixed shift 3.0. The scheduler steps **only the
target latents** (the model's output rows for the prefix are discarded).
VAE decode applies `z * std + mean` per channel; encode the inverse, and uses
the **posterior mode** (`argmax`), which keeps our seed-reproducibility rule
for free.

---

## What this changes about the vertical (semantics, not code)

- **Edits stop being SDEdit.** Today an edit is a truncated generation
  (strength ⇒ steps skipped ⇒ cheaper). In 2.1 an edit is a *conditional
  generation*: reference latents + vision context as prefix, target from pure
  noise, all 40 steps. An edit becomes **slightly more expensive** than a
  generation (bigger prefix), the `strength` knob disappears, and up to **10
  reference images** arrive (OpenAI's `image[]` array already allows several).
  `/v1/images/edits` keeps its shape; its documentation changes meaning.
- **RGBA is native.** The VAE emits 4 channels always; transparency is asked
  for in the prompt (the model card's recommended phrasing). Map OpenAI's
  `background: "transparent"` to that prompt prefix + PNG-with-alpha out;
  opaque requests composite over white.
- **Masked / annotated local edits** (circles, painted regions, separate
  masks) are a *capability the model has* — the current 501 for masks may
  become closable. How a separate mask is fed (extra condition image?) is not
  in the diffusers PR; needs the examples repo before promising it (open
  question Q-o3).
- **The cost profile inverts — now measured, no longer estimated.**
  Z-Image-Turbo was an 8-step distillation at 14.3 s an image; 2.1 wants 40
  steps, and Q4's GPU DiT measures **2.27 s a cached step, 2.29 s the
  prefill: 90.7 s of transformer per 1024² image** (the morning's estimate
  said ~70 s; the gap is unported fusions and the full-seq re-pack, priced
  under Q9). What a *served* image costs also needs the VAE's GPU stage
  (Q5g — the CPU decoder would add minutes) and the text encoder's ~1 s.
  2048² is still an estimate: GEMMs x4 and attention x16 over the 91 s.
  The two levers, in order: **the step count** (sweep 40/24/16/12 for
  quality — the knob exists, and at 2.27 s/step it is the difference between
  ~90 s and ~27 s) and **a distilled/turbo release or LoRA** (the ecosystem
  — lightx2v etc. — is where Z-Image-Turbo itself came from; watch for it).
  **Q6's sweep decides the served default**; 1024²/40 is the starting point,
  not a commitment.

## The preview problem (taef1 has no successor here)

`madebyollin/taehv`'s **taew2_1 does *not* fit this model**: it decodes the
Wan-2.1 16-channel/8x latent that the *original* Qwen-Image borrowed; 2.1's
VAE is a new 64-channel/16x RGBA design, and as of today taehv lists nothing
for it. So, in order:

1. **Q7 ships a fitted linear preview**: a 64→3 (or →4) matrix, least-squares
   over dumped (latent, 1/16-scale image) pairs — the latent2rgb approach.
   One GEMV per pixel, effectively free per step; a 1024² generation previews
   at 64x64, upscaled client-side. Fitting data comes out of Q0's dumps.
2. **Watch taehv** for a 2.1 variant and port it like `zimage/vae/tiny.go`
   (at T=1 its temporal machinery degenerates; it would be a small 2D conv
   stack again). Do not build our own distilled decoder — that is a training
   project this repo does not want.

## What survives, what is new, what dies

| piece | verdict |
|---|---|
| `zimage/qwen` (Qwen3 text transformer, CPU + GPU) | **survives and grows** — it is shared infra (`embed`, `llm`, `parakeet` import it). Q1 adds: theta as config (5e6), 36-layer/pre-final-norm output mode beside the existing `EncoderLayers()` convention, and (Q8 only) mrope + deepstack + the vision tower. The Qwen3-Embedding caller must keep passing its tests untouched. |
| `zimage/tokenizer` | **survives** — same BPE family; new `added_tokens.json` (`<image1>`…, vision markers) and the raw template above. |
| shaders: `dit_gemm_*`, `dit_attention_*` (WMMA), gpu arenas | **survived, confirmed by Q4** — the whole graph runs on z-image's kernels plus two new small shaders (`dit_attn_causal`, `dit_copy`). The new shapes run on z-image's measured winners *uncontested*: the tile re-screen at M=16384/K=12288 is a Q9 percent (hypothesis 5 in `TODO.md`). |
| `zimage/vae/gpu_conv*` | **survives as infrastructure** — the conv/groupnorm kernels feed the new VAE port. |
| `zimage/dit`, `zimage/vae` (model code), `zimage/pipeline` | **die** — replaced by a new `qimage/` tree (`qimage/dit`, `qimage/vae`, `qimage/pipeline`). New names because almost no line survives: different block, different mask, different VAE family. Delete z-image code as each Q-stage lands its replacement, not in one purge. |
| `cmd/zimage`, `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/vaebench`, … | retargeted to `qimage` equivalents as their stage arrives. |
| `models/Z-Image-Turbo`, `models/taef1` (62 GB) | delete from disk once Q6 serves — not before, so A/B stays possible. |
| serving: `/v1/images/*`, streaming, geometry-under-a-ceiling | **survives in shape** — I1/I2's design carries over; the adapter re-wires to `qimage/pipeline`. |

Two-machine deployment holds: image goes ~26 → **~36–40 GB resident**
(weights 32.3 GB fp16 + activations), sharing a 128 GB box with speech + TTS +
embeddings (~3 GB). Still no footprint quantisation.

  photorealistic render of the prompt. The env: the shared `.venv` with torch

## The five verticals, at a glance

All five of `GOALS.md`'s models run end to end in Go on Vulkan, validated
against a reference, and are served by `cmd/serve`. The competition from
here is our own ceiling, not a reference implementation.

| vertical | model | headline, measured | open |
|---|---|---|---|
| text generation | qwen3.8-flash-next (180 B, 6 B active) | decode **36.19 tok/s, 1.44x** llama.cpp at **+1.74%** perplexity; prefill **1213.5 tok/s at 8192 rows, 3.10x**, still climbing where llama.cpp plateaus | batching (P6); context depth; speculation parked at 0.95x |
| speech → text | parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 | an 11 s clip in **43 ms — 257x real time**, whole model resident | S10 front end (48% of the pipeline); S9 long clips |
| text → speech | Kokoro-82M | **31 ms for 3.25 s (105x)**, **162 ms for 19.5 s (120x)** — flat per second of audio; the endpoint answers in 59 ms | the vocoder's 20 ms of arithmetic; three small boundaries |
| image generation | Z-Image-Turbo | 1024², 8 steps in **14.3 s**; an edit **11.3 s**; first preview frame at **3.6 s** | 1.9 s of one fusion pattern in four places; the GEMMs' missing quarter |
| embeddings | Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | a text in **11.5 ms**, the card's similarity matrix to 1.3e-4 over HTTP | E7 batching, worth up to 10x on short texts |

**The server** (`API.md`): one process, one flag per vertical, OpenAI-shaped
(`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/audio/*`,
`/v1/images/*`, `/v1/embeddings`), plus a Wyoming door for Home Assistant
(`-wyoming`, byte-identical audio to the HTTP door). Everything unimplemented
is refused with a reason, never faked.

**Deployment is two machines**: the language model alone on one (~84 GB
resident), the other four verticals on the other (image ~26 GB, the rest
~3 GB together). `-llm` and `-image` do not fit in one 128 GB process, on
purpose — so no footprint quantisation is planned for the small verticals.

## The five verticals, at a glance

All five of `GOALS.md`'s models run end to end in Go on Vulkan, validated
against a reference, and are served by `cmd/serve`. The competition from
here is our own ceiling, not a reference implementation.

| vertical | model | headline, measured | open |
|---|---|---|---|
| text generation | qwen3.8-flash-next (180 B, 6 B active) | decode **36.19 tok/s, 1.44x** llama.cpp at **+1.74%** perplexity; prefill **1213.5 tok/s at 8192 rows, 3.10x**, still climbing where llama.cpp plateaus | batching (P6); context depth; speculation parked at 0.95x |
| speech → text | parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 | an 11 s clip in **43 ms — 257x real time**, whole model resident | S10 front end (48% of the pipeline); S9 long clips |
| text → speech | Kokoro-82M | **31 ms for 3.25 s (105x)**, **162 ms for 19.5 s (120x)** — flat per second of audio; the endpoint answers in 59 ms | the vocoder's 20 ms of arithmetic; three small boundaries |
| image generation | Z-Image-Turbo | 1024², 8 steps in **14.3 s**; an edit **11.3 s**; first preview frame at **3.6 s** | 1.9 s of one fusion pattern in four places; the GEMMs' missing quarter |
| embeddings | Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B | a text in **11.5 ms**, the card's similarity matrix to 1.3e-4 over HTTP | E7 batching, worth up to 10x on short texts |

**The server** (`API.md`): one process, one flag per vertical, OpenAI-shaped
(`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/audio/*`,
`/v1/images/*`, `/v1/embeddings`), plus a Wyoming door for Home Assistant
(`-wyoming`, byte-identical audio to the HTTP door). Everything unimplemented
is refused with a reason, never faked.

**Deployment is two machines**: the language model alone on one (~84 GB
resident), the other four verticals on the other (image ~26 GB, the rest
~3 GB together). `-llm` and `-image` do not fit in one 128 GB process, on
purpose — so no footprint quantisation is planned for the small verticals.

1	// Shared binding and push-constant layout for the VAE decoder shaders.
2	//
3	// Every decoder pipeline is built over the *same* four buffers and declares
4	// the *same* push-constant size, because vk.DispatchMultiTimed records a
5	// whole graph into one command buffer and requires that. A shader declares
6	// only the bindings it reads; the descriptors it does not name are inert.
7	// It is also the right shape for an engine: weights are one arena written
8	// once, activations are one arena the graph ping-pongs inside, and "which
9	// tensor" is an offset rather than a descriptor rebind.
10	//
11	// The decoder is fp32 except in the mid block, where stage 7 put the four
12	// projections and the attention on the matrix cores: those read two further
13	// bindings, an fp16 activation arena and an fp16 weight arena, and the
14	// shaders that do not use them simply leave them undeclared. Everything else
15	// is still the fp32 correctness port that had the CPU implementation in
16	// zimage/vae as its oracle.
17	
18	layout(binding = 0) readonly buffer Weights { float wbuf[]; };
19	layout(binding = 1) buffer Act { float act[]; };
20	
21	layout(push_constant) uniform PC {
22	    uint inOff;    // element offset of the input tensor in act
23	    uint outOff;   // element offset of the output tensor in act
24	    uint C;        // input channels
25	    uint H;        // input height
26	    uint W;        // input width
27	    uint OC;       // output channels
28	    uint KH;       // kernel height
29	    uint KW;       // kernel width
30	    uint pad;      // symmetric zero padding
31	    uint wOff;     // element offset of the weight tensor in wbuf
32	    uint bOff;     // element offset of the bias tensor in wbuf, or NO_BIAS
33	    uint groups;   // group count for group norm
34	    uint resOff;   // element offset of the residual/second operand in act

38	    // The GEMM block, mirroring shaders/dit_common.glsl field for field at
39	    // the same byte offsets. The attention projections run on
40	    // shaders/dit_gemm.comp *unmodified* -- it is a tuned kernel with three B
41	    // layouts and a grid swizzle behind it, and porting it onto a second

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5	
6		"strix-halo-vulkan/safetensors"
7		"strix-halo-vulkan/shaders"
8	)

10	// conv2d on the matrix cores -- PIPELINE.md stage 8.
11	//
12	// Stage 7 ended with the decode 85% one kernel: shaders/vae_conv2d.comp, 3.02
13	// s of a 3.62 s decode at 3.0-3.2 TFLOP/s against a 55.5 TFLOP/s fp16
14	// ceiling. It is the only operator in this pipeline that was never a GEMM
15	// with the wrong kernel in front of it -- its implicit GEMM had not been
16	// written -- and this file writes it.
17	//
18	// The shape of the answer was measured before any of it: stage 2 found the
19	// decoder's activations peak at absmax 497, 132x inside fp16, while the sums
20	// that reach 1.16e7 are the mid block's attention *scores*. So conv's
21	// operands narrow safely and its accumulators stay fp32, which is what a
22	// matrix core does natively. TestConvInputsFitFP16 is that measurement as an
23	// assertion rather than a memory.
24	//
25	// Two pieces, and the layout is the interesting one:
26	//
27	//   - shaders/vae_pack_conv.comp writes the activation as
28	//     [ceil(C/16)][H+2][W+2][16] -- 16 channels contiguous per pixel, with a
29	//     one-pixel zero border. That makes a B fragment (16 channels x 16
30	//     pixels) a 512 B contiguous column-major load *at any pixel offset*,
31	//     which is what a +-1 tap shift needs and what no tiling of the pixel
32	//     axis can give.
33	//   - shaders/vae_conv_wmma.comp is the implicit GEMM: C[OC, HW] = A[OC,
34	//     taps*C] * B[taps*C, HW], with B read through addresses rather than
35	//     materialised (im2col at 1024x1024 would be 4.7 GB) and A the filter,
36	//     packed once at load into the same 16x16 fragment tiles every WMMA
37	//     kernel in this engine has wanted since stage 3c.
38	//
39	// Every conv in the decoder goes through it, including the two shapes a
40	// tiled kernel would normally refuse: conv_out has three output channels and
41	// the 16x16 reference latent makes W as small as 16. The kernel's masked
42	// epilogue is what buys that, and it is worth the branch precisely because
43	// the tests run at those sizes -- a fast path the reference latent cannot
44	// reach is a fast path nothing checks.
45	
46	// ConvKernel names a build of shaders/vae_conv_wmma.comp, or stage 2b's
47	// scalar fp32 convolution.
48	type ConvKernel string
49	
50	const (
51		// ConvScalar is vae_conv2d.comp, the register-blocked fp32 kernel of
52		// stage 2b (research/stage-2-vae-decoder.md, IDEAS §2.1). It narrows
53		// nothing, so it stays the oracle the matrix-core path is measured
54		// against.
55		ConvScalar ConvKernel = "scalar"
56	
57		Conv64x64      ConvKernel = "64x64"
58		Conv64x64K2    ConvKernel = "64x64_k2"
59		Conv64x128     ConvKernel = "64x128"
60		Conv128x64     ConvKernel = "128x64"
61		Conv128x128    ConvKernel = "128x128"
62		Conv256x64     ConvKernel = "256x64"
63		Conv64x64W32   ConvKernel = "64x64_w32"
64		Conv128x64W32  ConvKernel = "128x64_w32"
65		Conv128x128W32 ConvKernel = "128x128_w32"
66	
67		// The negative controls. Both produce a wrong answer by construction:
68		// ConvNoTapShift drops the horizontal tap offset, and ConvPadClamp
69		// replicates the edge pixel instead of zeroing the border. They are
70		// selectable but are not in the ladder, because a ladder is a measurement
71		// and a build that computes the wrong answer has nothing to contribute
72		// to one.
73		ConvNoTapShift ConvKernel = "no_tap_shift"
74		ConvPadClamp   ConvKernel = "pad_clamp"
75	)
76	
77	// DefaultConvKernel is the ladder's winner at a 1024x1024 image: 258 ms and
78	// 38.3 TFLOP/s, against the 3.18 s and 3.1 TFLOP/s of the kernel it replaces.
79	// It ties with Conv128x128W32 to within the noise at that size and is taken
80	// over it for the small ones, where a 64-wide tile leaves fewer waves idle on
81	// a 16-pixel row. See research/stage-8-vae-conv.md.
82	const DefaultConvKernel = Conv128x64W32
83	
84	// convVariant is what the host has to know that the SPIR-V does not carry:
85	// the workgroup's output tile, because it sets the grid, and the wave size,
86	// because the kernel maps gl_SubgroupID onto a wave grid and a workgroup
87	// holding the wrong number of waves would write outside its tile.
88	type convVariant struct {
89		name   ConvKernel
90		spirv  []byte
91		bm, bn int
92		waves  int
93		wave   uint32
94		// pack overrides the packing pass, which only a control does.
95		pack []byte
96	}
97	
98	// packSpirv is the pass that feeds this build.
99	func (v convVariant) packSpirv() []byte {
100		if v.pack != nil {
101			return v.pack
102		}
103		return shaders.VAEPackConv
104	}
105	
106	var convVariants = []convVariant{
107		{name: Conv64x64, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA64x64, bm: 64, bn: 64, waves: 1, wave: 64},
108		{name: Conv64x64K2, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA64x64K2, bm: 64, bn: 64, waves: 1, wave: 64},
109		{name: Conv64x128, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA64x128, bm: 64, bn: 128, waves: 2, wave: 64},
110		{name: Conv128x64, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA128x64, bm: 128, bn: 64, waves: 2, wave: 64},
111		{name: Conv128x128, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA128x128, bm: 128, bn: 128, waves: 4, wave: 64},
112		{name: Conv256x64, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA256x64, bm: 256, bn: 64, waves: 4, wave: 64},
113		{name: Conv64x64W32, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA64x64W32, bm: 64, bn: 64, waves: 1, wave: 32},
114		{name: Conv128x64W32, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA128x64W32, bm: 128, bn: 64, waves: 2, wave: 32},
115		{name: Conv128x128W32, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA128x128W32, bm: 128, bn: 128, waves: 4, wave: 32},
116	}
117	
118	var convControls = []convVariant{
119		{name: ConvNoTapShift, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMANoTapShift, bm: 128, bn: 128, waves: 4, wave: 64},
120		{name: ConvPadClamp, spirv: shaders.VAEConvWMMA128x128, bm: 128, bn: 128, waves: 4, wave: 64,
121			pack: shaders.VAEPackConvClamp},
122	}
123	
124	// ConvKernels lists every build in the ladder, in the order they are
125	// measured. The controls are not in it.
126	func ConvKernels() []ConvKernel {
127		out := []ConvKernel{ConvScalar}
128		for _, v := range convVariants {
129			out = append(out, v.name)
130		}
131		return out
132	}
133	
134	func convVariantFor(k ConvKernel) (convVariant, bool) {
135		for _, v := range convVariants {
136			if v.name == k {
137				return v, true
138			}
139		}
140		for _, v := range convControls {
141			if v.name == k {
142				return v, true
143			}
144		}
145		return convVariant{}, false
146	}
147	
148	// convBorder is the one-pixel zero frame the packed layout carries on every
149	// side. It is what makes the nine taps branchless: every address the kernel
150	// forms holds either a real activation or a zero, so the convolution's
151	// padding is in the data rather than in the inner loop.
152	const convBorder = 1
153	
154	func ctiles(c int) int { return (c + coopMatTile - 1) / coopMatTile }
155	
156	// convPadW is the packed layout's row width, and the floor is the whole of
157	// what it says. The kernel clamps every pixel address to the last whole
158	// fragment of its channel plane so that nothing it forms can leave the
159	// buffer; that fragment is the tail of the bottom border row and must
160	// therefore be sixteen zeros. At a row narrower than sixteen it would not be
161	// -- it would reach back into the last real row -- which is a bug the
162	// 1024x1024 image cannot have and the 96x96 one the tests decode does.
163	func convPadW(w int) int { return max(w+2*convBorder, coopMatTile) }
164	
165	// packedConvElems is the size, in halves, of a tensor's blocked fp16 form.
166	func packedConvElems(c, h, w int) int {
167		return ctiles(c) * coopMatTile * (h + 2*convBorder) * convPadW(w)
168	}
169	
170	// packConvA narrows one filter into the A-operand fragment tiles
171	// vae_conv_wmma.comp reads: tile (mt, kt) is 256 contiguous halves holding
172	// element (oc, k) at (oc%16)*16 + k%16, tiles ordered kt-fastest, with
173	// k = tap*ceil(InC/16)*16 + ic.
174	//
175	// The k axis is tap-major so that a k-tile is 16 input channels at *one*
176	// tap, which is what lets the kernel hold the tap loop outside and form one
177	// pixel address per tap rather than per k-tile. Both the channel axis and
178	// the output-channel axis are padded to 16 with zeros, so an InC of 16
179	// (conv_in) and an OutC of 3 (conv_out) are a padded K and a masked store
180	// rather than two special cases.
181	func packConvA(dst []uint16, w []float32, oc, ic, taps int) {
182		ct := ctiles(ic)
183		kt := ct * taps
184		for o := 0; o < oc; o++ {
185			mt, lane := o/coopMatTile, (o%coopMatTile)*coopMatTile
186			for t := 0; t < taps; t++ {
187				for c := 0; c < ic; c++ {
188					k := t*ct*coopMatTile + c
189					dst[(mt*kt+k/coopMatTile)*coopMatTile*coopMatTile+lane+k%coopMatTile] =
190						safetensors.F32ToF16(w[(o*ic+c)*taps+t])
191				}
192			}
193		}
194	}
195	
196	// convWeightElems is how many halves packConvA writes for one filter.
197	func convWeightElems(c *Conv2D) int {
198		return ctiles(c.OutC) * ctiles(c.InC) * c.KH * c.KW * coopMatTile * coopMatTile
199	}
200	
201	// expandBias repeats each output channel's bias across a 16-wide row, so
202	// that one row-major accumulator load of stride 16 broadcasts it over a
203	// fragment's sixteen pixels. That is the whole of the bias handling: the
204	// kernel *starts* from it instead of adding it, which costs no dispatch, no
205	// epilogue and nothing in the inner loop. The 16x it costs is 32 KB on the
206	// widest conv in this decoder.
207	func expandBias(bias []float32, oc int) []float32 {
208		out := make([]float32, ctiles(oc)*coopMatTile*coopMatTile)
209		for o := 0; o < oc; o++ {
210			for i := 0; i < coopMatTile; i++ {
211				out[o*coopMatTile+i] = bias[o]
212			}
213		}
214		return out
215	}
216	
217	// stageConvWeights appends every conv filter to the fp16 weight arena in its
218	// fragment-tile layout. For the full decoder this is 84 M parameters -- the
219	// whole of it -- so unlike stage 7's four projections it is worth saying what
220	// it costs: 168 MB of fp16 beside the 336 MB of fp32 the scalar path still
221	// reads for the convs it keeps. Nothing is freed, because the fp32 copy is
222	// what TestGPUConvMatchesScalar compares against and what a device without
223	// matrix cores runs.
224	//
225	// It is on the engine rather than on either decoder because the packed layout
226	// is the engine's: taef1 stages its 1.2 M parameters through the same call.
227	func (e *engine) stageConvWeights(data []uint16) []uint16 {
228		for _, cr := range e.convs {
229			off := uint32(len(data))
230			data = append(data, make([]uint16, convWeightElems(cr.conv))...)
231			packConvA(data[off:], cr.conv.Weight, cr.conv.OutC, cr.conv.InC, cr.conv.KH*cr.conv.KW)
232			e.w16[cr.name+".weight"] = off
233		}
234		return data
235	}
236	
237	// packConv records the fp32 -> blocked-fp16 pass in front of one convolution
238	// and returns the packed tensor's offset in the fp16 arena.
239	//
240	// It is a read of the activation and a write of half of it -- 7 ms at the
241	// largest shape in the decode against the 30 the convolution it feeds should
242	// take -- and it is the price of the layout. The cheaper form is to have the
243	// producer write it (every conv in a resnet is fed by a SiLU), which is a
244	// fusion this stage leaves on the table rather than one it needs.
245	func (b *builder) packConv(x tensor) uint32 {
246		off := b.har.alloc(packedConvElems(x.C, x.H, x.W))
247		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("packconv %dx%dx%d", x.C, x.H, x.W), 0)
248		b.add("pack_conv", uint32(ctiles(x.C)*(x.H+2*convBorder)), pushConstants{
249			InOff: x.off, OutOff: off,
250			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
251			Aux1: uint32(convPadW(x.W)),
252		})
253		return off
254	}
255	
256	// convCores records one convolution on the matrix cores: the pack, then the
257	// implicit GEMM.
258	//
259	// The grid is (H * ceil(W/BN), ceil(OC/BM)). A pixel tile never straddles two
260	// image rows -- a tap shift would wrap the wrong pixels in -- so the x axis
261	// carries the row as well as the tile, and the shader is told how many tiles
262	// a row holds rather than dividing by a constant it does not have.
263	func (b *builder) convCores(name string, c *Conv2D, x tensor) tensor {
264		v := b.e.conv
265		out := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(c.OutC * x.H * x.W), C: c.OutC, H: x.H, W: x.W}
266		packed := b.packConv(x)
267		tilesPerRow := (x.W + v.bn - 1) / v.bn
268		b.label(convLabel(c, x), convFlops(c, x))
269		b.addXY("conv_wmma", uint32(x.H*tilesPerRow), uint32((c.OutC+v.bm-1)/v.bm), pushConstants{
270			InOff: packed, OutOff: out.off,
271			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
272			OC: uint32(c.OutC), KH: uint32(c.KH), KW: uint32(c.KW), Pad: uint32(c.Pad),
273			BOff:  b.convBiasOff(name),
274			GemmB: b.b16Off(name + ".weight"),
275			Aux0:  uint32(tilesPerRow), Aux1: uint32(convPadW(x.W)),
276		})
277		b.har.release(packed, packedConvElems(x.C, x.H, x.W))
278		return out
279	}
280	
281	// convBiasOff resolves the expanded bias, or NO_BIAS. A conv without one is
282	// not a case this decoder has, but there is no push-constant value that means
283	// "not set" (stage 6), so it is said rather than assumed.
284	func (b *builder) convBiasOff(name string) uint32 {
285		if off, ok := b.e.weights.off[name+".bias16"]; ok {
286			return off
287		}
288		return noBias
289	}
290	
291	func convLabel(c *Conv2D, x tensor) string {
292		return fmt.Sprintf("conv%dx%d %d->%d @%dx%d", c.KH, c.KW, x.C, c.OutC, x.H, x.W)
293	}
294	
295	func convFlops(c *Conv2D, x tensor) float64 {
296		return 2 * float64(c.OutC) * float64(x.H) * float64(x.W) * float64(x.C) *
297			float64(c.KH) * float64(c.KW)
298	}

12	// The mid block on the matrix cores -- PIPELINE.md stage 7.
13	//
14	// Stage 2b's decoder is fp32 everywhere and its attention block is the two
15	// slowest things in a 1024x1024 decode: the softmax over 16384 pixels is
16	// **1.42 s in one dispatch, 26%** of the image, and the four 512x512
17	// projections another 544 ms at **62 GFLOP/s**, which is 0.1% of what this
18	// part's matrix cores do. Both are GEMMs in the end, and the engine already
19	// has a tuned one.
20	//
21	// So this file is mostly plumbing around two reuses:
22	//
23	//   - the projections run on shaders/dit_gemm.comp *unmodified*, which is why
24	//     vae_common.glsl's push-constant block mirrors dit_common.glsl's GEMM
25	//     fields at the same offsets. Forking a kernel that carries §2.1, §2.3,
26	//     §2.4 and §2.7 behind it to rename six fields would be the wrong trade.
27	//   - the weights are staged as 16x16 fragment tiles, which stage 4a measured
28	//     at 1.46x on the DiT's projections and which costs nothing here: a VAE
29	//     weight is packed once at load and read every decode.
30	//
31	// The attention kernel is the one thing that could not be reused --
32	// shaders/vae_attention_wmma.comp says why -- and the fp16 activations it
33	// wants are produced by two small passes, a row-major narrowing for the GEMM
34	// operands and a fragment-tile pack for q, k and v.
35	//
36	// The fp32 path is kept and is what the fp16 one is tested against
37	// (gpu_test.go). It is also the fallback: a device without fp16 storage,
38	// cooperative matrices or subgroup-size control runs the whole decoder
39	// exactly as stage 2b left it.

41	// AttnKernel names a build of shaders/vae_attention_wmma.comp, or the fp32
42	// kernel of stage 2b.
43	type AttnKernel string
44	
45	const (
46		// AttnScalar is vae_attention.comp, the two-pass fp32 kernel. It stays
47		// the oracle: it never narrows anything, so a disagreement between it and
48		// a matrix-core build is the matrix-core build's.
49		AttnScalar AttnKernel = "scalar"
50	
51		AttnQT1KT2    AttnKernel = "qt1_kt2"
52		AttnQT1KT4    AttnKernel = "qt1_kt4"
53		AttnQT1KT8    AttnKernel = "qt1_kt8"
54		AttnQT2KT2    AttnKernel = "qt2_kt2"
55		AttnQT1KT2W32 AttnKernel = "qt1_kt2_w32"
56		AttnQT1KT4W32 AttnKernel = "qt1_kt4_w32"
57	
58		// The negative controls. Both produce a wrong answer by construction and
59		// exist so that the tolerance the right answer is held to has been shown
60		// to catch something.
61		AttnNoCrossWave AttnKernel = "no_cross_wave"
62		AttnNoRescale   AttnKernel = "no_rescale"
63	)

65	// DefaultAttnKernel is the ladder's winner at a 1024x1024 image: 15.1 ms and
66	// 36.4 TFLOP/s, against 23.6 for the same tiling at wave64. See
67	// research/stage-7-vae-mid-block.md.
68	const DefaultAttnKernel = AttnQT1KT4W32
69	
70	// attnVariant is what the host has to know about a build that the SPIR-V does
71	// not carry: the two tile knobs, because they set the grid and the padding,
72	// and the wave size, because a multi-wave workgroup has to have it pinned --
73	// at wave32 the workgroup would hold twice the waves the kernel maps onto its
74	// component axis and half of them would write outside it.

76		name  AttnKernel
77		spirv []byte
78		qt    int // query tiles per workgroup
79		ktil  int // key tiles per block
80		wave  uint32
81	}

83	var attnVariants = []attnVariant{
84		{AttnQT1KT4, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMAQT1KT4, 1, 4, 64},
85		{AttnQT1KT2, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMAQT1KT2, 1, 2, 64},
86		{AttnQT1KT8, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMAQT1KT8, 1, 8, 64},
87		{AttnQT2KT2, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMAQT2KT2, 2, 2, 64},
88		{AttnQT1KT2W32, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMAQT1KT2W32, 1, 2, 32},
89		{AttnQT1KT4W32, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMAQT1KT4W32, 1, 4, 32},
90		{AttnNoCrossWave, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMANoCrossWave, 1, 4, 64},
91		{AttnNoRescale, shaders.VAEAttentionWMMANoRescale, 1, 4, 64},
92	}

94	// AttnKernels lists every build in the ladder, in the order they are measured.

97		for _, v := range attnVariants {
98			out = append(out, v.name)
99		}

107			}

113	// arms are offered: the weight is packed once at load, so the layout that
114	// costs the DiT a pass per step costs the VAE nothing, and stage 4a measured
115	// every other arm behind it.
116	type GEMMKernel string

119		GEMMWG128x256 GEMMKernel = "wg128x256_bt16_swz8"
120		GEMMReg64     GEMMKernel = "reg64_bt16"
121		GEMMReg64HKA4 GEMMKernel = "reg64_hka4_bt16"

123	)

126	// See research/stage-7-vae-mid-block.md.

161	const (

164		// in the M direction. dit_gemm.comp has no bounds check -- it writes whole

166		// attention kernel's key blocks (at most 8 tiles) divide it.
167		gemmRowAlign = 128

174	func padRows(rows int) int { return (rows + gemmRowAlign - 1) &^ (gemmRowAlign - 1) }

176	// hasMatrixCores reports whether a device can run the fp16 path at all. The
177	// decoder falls back to stage 2b's kernels rather than failing, because every
178	// stage of this pipeline still has an fp32 answer and a device that cannot do
179	// coopmat should still decode.
180	func hasMatrixCores(dev *vk.Device) bool {
181		f := dev.Features()
182		if !f.Float16 || !f.CoopMatrix || !f.SubgroupSizeControl {
183			return false
184		}
185		sgs, err := dev.Physical().SubgroupSizeControl()
186		return err == nil && sgs.Supported && sgs.MinSubgroupSize <= 32 && sgs.MaxSubgroupSize >= 64

189	// packTiledB narrows a [n, k] row-major PyTorch weight into the 16x16
190	// fragment tiles dit_gemm.comp's B_LAYOUT=2 reads: tile (nt, kt) is 256
191	// contiguous halves holding element (k, n) at (n%16)*16 + k%16, tiles ordered
192	// kt-fastest so one n-tile's whole K row is contiguous. This is zimage/dit's
193	// packB, layout 2, without the chunking -- the VAE has four 512x512 weights
194	// where the DiT has 6.0e9 elements.
195	func packTiledB(dst []uint16, w []float32, n, k int) {
196		kt := k / coopMatTile
197		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
198			row := w[i*k : (i+1)*k]
199			base := (i / coopMatTile) * kt * coopMatTile * coopMatTile
200			lane := (i % coopMatTile) * coopMatTile
201			for j, v := range row {
202				dst[base+(j/coopMatTile)*coopMatTile*coopMatTile+lane+j%coopMatTile] = safetensors.F32ToF16(v)

204		}
205	}

208	// weight arena. Nothing else in either direction's graph is narrowed this way:
209	// these are the only tensors dit_gemm.comp reads.

212	// same 512 channels at the same latent resolution -- and both stage it under
213	// the same four names.
214	func (g *engine) stageProjections(data []uint16, a *Attention) []uint16 {
215		put := func(name string, l *Linear) {
216			off := uint32(len(data))
217			data = append(data, make([]uint16, l.Out*l.In)...)
218			packTiledB(data[off:], l.Weight, l.Out, l.In)
219			g.w16[name] = off
220		}
221		put("mid.attn.q", a.Q)
222		put("mid.attn.k", a.K)
223		put("mid.attn.v", a.V)
224		put("mid.attn.out", a.Out)

231		off := b.har.alloc(rowsPad * lda)
232		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("narrow %dx%d", rows, in.C), 0)
233		b.add("narrow", uint32(rowsPad), pushConstants{

243	// weight. The bias is not here -- dit_gemm.comp has none, and every one of

247	// to be part of what the arena reclaims.
248	func (b *builder) proj(name string, l *Linear, aOff uint32, rows, rowsPad, lda int) tensor {
249		v := b.e.gemm
250		out := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rowsPad * l.Out), C: l.Out, H: rowsPad, W: 1}
251		b.label(fmt.Sprintf("gemm %d->%d x%d", l.In, l.Out, rows),

253		b.addXY("gemm", uint32(l.Out/v.bn), uint32(rowsPad/v.bm), pushConstants{
254			InOff: aOff, OutOff: out.off,

256			GemmN: uint32(l.Out), GemmK: uint32(l.In),
257			LDA: uint32(lda),

260	}

268			Aux0: uint32(rows), Aux1: math.Float32bits(scale), Aux2: bias,
269		})

273	// its softmax on vae_attention_wmma.comp. Same graph as builder.attention,
274	// dispatch for dispatch, except that the scalar kernel's K transpose is
275	// subsumed by the pack (a tile of k is stored the same way as a tile of q,
276	// because both matmuls reduce over the component axis) and two narrowings
277	// appear, which is what fp16 operands cost.
278	func (b *builder) attentionWMMA(name string, a *Attention, x tensor) tensor {
279		rows := x.H * x.W
280		dim := a.Q.Out
281		rowsPad := padRows(rows)
282		lda := dim + gemmPad
283	
284		h := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(x.elems()), C: x.C, H: x.H, W: x.W}
285		b.add("groupnorm", uint32(a.GroupNorm.Groups), pushConstants{
286			InOff: x.off, OutOff: h.off,
287			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
288			WOff: b.wOff(name + ".norm.weight"), BOff: b.wOff(name + ".norm.bias"),
289			Groups: uint32(a.GroupNorm.Groups), Aux0: math.Float32bits(float32(a.GroupNorm.Eps)),
290		})
291	
292		seq := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rows * x.C), C: x.C, H: x.H, W: x.W}
293		b.add("to_rows", groups(rows*x.C, 256), pushConstants{
294			InOff: h.off, OutOff: seq.off,
295			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
296		})
297	
298		hA := b.narrow(seq, rows, rowsPad, lda)
299		q := b.proj(name+".q", a.Q, hA, rows, rowsPad, lda)
300		k := b.proj(name+".k", a.K, hA, rows, rowsPad, lda)
301		v := b.proj(name+".v", a.V, hA, rows, rowsPad, lda)
302		b.har.release(hA, rowsPad*lda)

304		// The packed planes are addressed in tiles and padded to the workgroup
305		// tile, so the key loop can read whole blocks past the last real row: a
306		// pad row is zeroed, and a zero key scores zero, which the kernel then
307		// masks out of the denominator anyway.

311		// is exp2, which is one instruction on this ISA.
312		const log2e = 1.4426950408889634
313		b.pack("pack", "pack q", q, hQ, rows, rowsPad, b.bOff(name+".q.bias"), float32(a.Scale*log2e))
314		b.pack("pack", "pack k", k, hK, rows, rowsPad, b.bOff(name+".k.bias"), 1)
315		b.pack("packt", "pack v", v, hV, rows, rowsPad, b.bOff(name+".v.bias"), 1)
316	
317		ctx := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(rowsPad * dim), C: dim, H: rowsPad, W: 1}

320		b.add("attn_wmma", uint32((rows+b.e.attn.qt*coopMatTile-1)/(b.e.attn.qt*coopMatTile)), pushConstants{

322			C:    uint32(dim),
323			Aux0: uint32(rows),
324		})
325		b.har.release(hQ, plane)
326		b.har.release(hK, plane)
327		b.har.release(hV, plane)
328	
329		hCtx := b.narrow(ctx, rows, rowsPad, lda)
330		outRows := b.proj(name+".out", a.Out, hCtx, rows, rowsPad, lda)
331		b.har.release(hCtx, rowsPad*lda)
332	
333		res := tensor{off: b.ar.alloc(x.elems()), C: x.C, H: x.H, W: x.W}
334		b.add("to_nchw", groups(x.elems(), 256), pushConstants{

336			C: uint32(x.C), H: uint32(x.H), W: uint32(x.W),
337			Aux0: b.bOff(name + ".out.bias"),
338		})
