**The end-to-end image gate Q3 owed is closed**: `TestEndToEndImage` runs
  prompt → image through our tokenizer, text encoder, DiT, scheduler and
  decoder — only the noise is the oracle's — and matches the 256²/4-step
  reference image at **max abs 9.1e-4, mean 6e-6** in [0, 1] space, 24x
  inside the 2.2e-2 precedent. (~65 GB fp32 passes through, sequenced to a
  ~34 GB peak; it must run alone.)
- **Q5g — the decoder on the GPU. Done 2026-09-20** (`qimage/vae/gpu.go`,
  ~700 lines): **1024² decodes in 7.36 / 7.77 s** over 117 dispatches, and
  256² in 0.38 s against the CPU port's ~20 s. Gated stagewise against
  `out/qi21vae` on **vae_test.go's own bounds, unchanged** — conv_in through
  every up block at rel 1e-5–4e-5, the image at **max abs 7.3e-4** (s256)
  and 7.8e-4 (192x320), both under the CPU port's own 8.7e-4 — plus a direct
  GPU-vs-CPU decode at **max abs 4.9e-4** and a negative control (every
  DupUp temporal factor set to 1) caught at **18443x the bound**.
  The port is small because z-image's decoder graph and six of its kernels
  carry over unchanged; three things in this VAE are not in that one, and
  each is one shader: `qvae_chnorm` (the per-pixel channel L2 norm, with the
  SiLU that always follows it fused in), `qvae_dupup` (the up blocks'
  parameter-free shortcut, whose channel mapping still depends on a temporal
  factor with no axis left), and a `-DDIM=1152` build of the scalar
  attention, whose query row and context live in shared memory. The mid
  block's projections are `to_qkv`'s three row blocks read at offsets — a
  1x1 convolution is a linear over the pixel rows — so there is no qkv
  convolution in the dispatch list.
  **Q0's fp16 constraint turned out to bind one convolution, not the
  graph** (`TestConvInputRanges`, the permanent instrument): the channel
  norm in front of every resnet convolution bounds what it reads, so **43 of
  44 convolutions peak below 1.1e4** and only the `288→144` 1x1 shortcut in
  up_blocks.4 — reading the raw residual at **absmax 2.6e5** — is outside
  fp16. That is what prices Q9's matrix-core port, below.
  **The encoder stays on the CPU**: nothing t2i serves needs it, and its
  stride-2 asymmetric-pad downsampler is a kernel the decoder's graph does
  not have. It belongs with Q8(a), which is the first thing that wants it.
- **Q6 — serve t2i.** Unblocked. `-image` loads qimage;
  `/v1/images/generations` with geometry under a ceiling (multiples of 32
  now, not 16), `background: "transparent"`, steps default 40. **First
  honest served wall clock** (two runs), the free-run image eyeball Q4
  deferred here, and the **step-count sweep** (40/24/16/12, same seed, a
  fixed prompt set) that decides the served default. Delete Z-Image weights
  and dead code after this lands.
  **The ceiling is now a number, and it is not 2048²**: the activation arena
  is one storage buffer, this device caps one at `maxStorageBufferRange` =
  4 GiB − 4, and the decode needs **3060 MB at 1024², 4090 MB at 1184² and
  4315 MB at 1216²** (`TestArenaCeiling`). So **1184² is the largest square
  this decoder decodes**, against a model whose own README examples are
  2048². Closing that is a capability, not a percent, and there are two
  routes: tiled decode (what diffusers' `enable_tiling` does, and the up
  blocks are local enough for it) or splitting the arena across several
  buffers bound as a descriptor array — `vk.PipelineSpec.Counts` already
  exists for exactly this, and the LLM's 77 GB bank is the precedent.

content.text:
Q5g is done — the serving blocker is cleared.

## What landed

**`qimage/vae/gpu.go`** (~700 lines) + two new shaders. The 1024² decode that would have cost minutes on the CPU runs on the device in **7.4 s** (two runs: 7.39 / 7.49 s), 117 dispatches; 256² in 0.38 s.

The port is small because z-image's decoder graph and six of its kernels carry over unchanged. Three things in this VAE genuinely aren't in that one, one shader each:
- `qvae_chnorm.comp` — the per-pixel L2-across-channels norm (not a group norm), with the SiLU that always follows it fused in
- `qvae_dupup.comp` — the up blocks' parameter-free shortcut, whose channel mapping still depends on a temporal factor that has no axis left at T=1
- a `-DDIM=1152` build of `vae_attention.comp` (its query row and context live in shared memory, so the width is compile-time). The default 512 build is byte-identical; `zimage/vae`'s GPU tests still pass.

The mid block's projections are `to_qkv`'s three row blocks read at offsets — a 1x1 conv is a linear over pixel rows — so there's no qkv convolution in the dispatch list.

## Gates

Stagewise against `out/qi21vae` on **vae_test.go's bounds unchanged**: up blocks at rel 1e-5–4e-5, the image at max abs **7.3e-4** (s256) / 7.8e-4 (192x320), both under the CPU port's own 8.7e-4. Direct GPU-vs-CPU decode: **4.9e-4**. Negative control (every DupUp `FactorT` forced to 1) caught at **18443x the bound**.

## Two measurements that change the plan

**Q0's fp16 constraint binds one convolution, not the graph.** The channel norm in front of every resnet conv bounds what it reads, so 43 of 44 convs peak below 1.1e4 — only the `288→144` 1x1 shortcut in up_blocks.4, reading the raw residual at absmax 2.6e5, is outside fp16. So z-image's matrix-core conv *can* take **every conv3x3**, which is 68.8% / 5.13 s at 3.2 TFLOP/s — the same starting point that stage 8 took to 258 ms. Priced under Q9 with the projections (21%, 1.57 s on the naive `linear`); together ~7.4 s → ~1.3 s.

**2048² is not a flag away.** The arena is one storage buffer, capped at 4 GiB−4 here: 3060 MB at 1024², 4090 MB at 1184², 4315 MB at 1216². **1184² is the largest square this decoder decodes**, against a model whose README examples are 2048². That's a capability gap, not a percent — tiled decode, or a multi-buffer arena via `vk.PipelineSpec.Counts`. I amended decision 4 in IMAGE.md rather than leaving it saying 2048² was pending numbers.

**Left out deliberately**: the encoder stays on the CPU. Nothing t2i serves needs it, and its stride-2 asymmetric-pad downsampler is a kernel this graph doesn't have — it belongs with Q8(a), which is the first thing that wants it. IMAGE.md now says so.

2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"math/rand"

7	
8		"strix-halo-vulkan/qimage/dit"
9		"strix-halo-vulkan/qimage/textenc"

11		"strix-halo-vulkan/safetensors"
12		"strix-halo-vulkan/vk"
13		"strix-halo-vulkan/zimage/qwen"
14		"strix-halo-vulkan/zimage/tokenizer"
15		zvae "strix-halo-vulkan/zimage/vae"
16	)
17	
18	// The resident text-to-image pipeline — IMAGE.md Q6.
19	//
20	// Three staged models and nothing else: Q1's text encoder (zimage/qwen's
21	// GPUEncoder over the Qwen3-VL config), Q4's DiT, and Q5g's VAE decoder.
22	// Everything between them is arithmetic the host does per request — the
23	// template, the token drop, the layout, the schedule, the packing — so a
24	// request names a size and a step count rather than choosing a process.
25	//
26	// **The resolution is not part of what is resident.** The three arenas are
27	// sized once for the ceiling the flags asked for; a smaller image is the
28	// same three graphs with smaller numbers in them. That is the same split
29	// z-image's pipeline made and the same one api.ImageBackend's Geometry()
30	// expects: a size is a request parameter, a ceiling is residency.
31	//
32	// **The ceiling is the VAE's, and it is 1184², not 2048².** The decoder's
33	// activation arena is one storage buffer and this device caps one at 4 GiB
34	// − 4 (qimage/vae's TestArenaCeiling). New refuses a larger ceiling here,
35	// naming the number, rather than letting a buffer allocation fail three
36	// models into staging.
37	
38	const (
39		// SizeMultiple is what both sides of an image must be a multiple of: the
40		// VAE is 16x spatial and the VLM groups latent tokens 2x2, so a latent
41		// grid has to be even on both axes.
42		SizeMultiple = 32
43		// VAEScale is how much larger the image is than the latent grid.
44		VAEScale = 16
45	
46		// DefaultSteps is the checkpoint's own default schedule. Unlike
47		// Z-Image-Turbo's 8, this is not a distillation — 2.1 is a full model and
48		// 40 is what diffusers runs.
49		DefaultSteps = 40
50		// DefaultSize is the pipeline's default resolution, which is also
51		// diffusers' (the README's examples use 2048² explicitly instead).
52		DefaultSize = 1024
53		// DefaultMaxPrompt is the text encoder's token ceiling. A t2i prompt is
54		// the template plus the user's text, tens of tokens in practice.
55		DefaultMaxPrompt = 512
56	)
57	
58	// Options is what cmd/serve's flags come to.
59	type Options struct {
60		// Model is the Qwen-Image-2.1 checkpoint root, holding transformer/,
61		// text_encoder/, vae/, processor/ and scheduler/.
62		Model string
63		// Width and Height are the largest image the arenas are built for, and
64		// the size a request that names none gets.
65		Width, Height int
66		// Steps is the schedule a request that names none gets.
67		Steps int
68		// MaxPrompt is the longest prompt the text encoder is built for.
69		MaxPrompt int
70	}
71	
72	// geom is a resolved size, all the way down to the transformer's row count.
73	type geom struct {
74		width, height    int
75		latentH, latentW int
76		imgTokens        int
77	}
78	
79	func newGeom(width, height int) (geom, error) {
80		if width <= 0 || height <= 0 {
81			return geom{}, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: %dx%d is not an image", width, height)
82		}
83		if width%SizeMultiple != 0 || height%SizeMultiple != 0 {
84			return geom{}, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: %dx%d; both sides must be a multiple of %d",
85				width, height, SizeMultiple)
86		}
87		g := geom{width: width, height: height, latentH: height / VAEScale, latentW: width / VAEScale}
88		g.imgTokens = g.latentH * g.latentW
89		return g, nil
90	}
91	
92	// Pipeline is the three staged models plus what a request needs to drive
93	// them. One image at a time: the arenas are one image's.
94	type Pipeline struct {
95		opt Options
96	
97		tok  *tokenizer.Tokenizer
98		drop int
99		enc  *qwen.GPUEncoder
100		dt   *dit.GPU
101		dec  *qvae.GPUDecoder
102		vcfg *qvae.Config
103		scfg *SchedConfig
104	
105		def, max geom
106		steps    int
107	
108		// residency, for the startup banner.
109		encBytes, ditBytes, vaeBytes, actBytes int
110	}
111	
112	// New stages the whole pipeline on the device.
113	func New(dev *vk.Device, opt Options) (*Pipeline, error) {
114		if opt.Width == 0 && opt.Height == 0 {
115			opt.Width, opt.Height = DefaultSize, DefaultSize
116		}
117		if opt.Width == 0 {
118			opt.Width = opt.Height
119		}
120		if opt.Height == 0 {
121			opt.Height = opt.Width
122		}
123		if opt.Steps == 0 {
124			opt.Steps = DefaultSteps
125		}
126		if opt.MaxPrompt == 0 {
127			opt.MaxPrompt = DefaultMaxPrompt
128		}
129		max, err := newGeom(opt.Width, opt.Height)
130		if err != nil {
131			return nil, err
132		}
133	
134		p := &Pipeline{opt: opt, def: max, max: max, steps: opt.Steps}
135	
136		// The tokenizer and the two configs first: they are cheap, and a
137		// checkpoint that is missing a piece should say so before 30 GB of
138		// staging rather than after.
139		if p.tok, err = tokenizer.Load(opt.Model + "/processor"); err != nil {
140			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: tokenizer: %w", err)
141		}
142		if p.drop, err = textenc.DropTokens(p.tok); err != nil {
143			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: system-message length: %w", err)
144		}
145		tcfg, err := textenc.LoadConfig(opt.Model + "/text_encoder")
146		if err != nil {
147			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: text encoder config: %w", err)
148		}
149		if p.vcfg, err = qvae.LoadConfig(opt.Model + "/vae"); err != nil {
150			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: VAE config: %w", err)
151		}
152		if p.scfg, err = LoadSchedConfig(opt.Model + "/scheduler"); err != nil {
153			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: scheduler config: %w", err)
154		}
155	
156		// The VAE's ceiling, checked before anything is staged. It is a property
157		// of the graph and the device, so it costs a plan rather than an
158		// allocation — and the alternative is a caller discovering it from a
159		// failed 12 GB buffer after the other two models are already resident.
160		cpuDec, err := qvae.LoadDecoder(opt.Model+"/vae", p.vcfg)
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: VAE decoder: %w", err)
163		}
164		need, err := qvae.ArenaBytes(cpuDec, max.latentH, max.latentW)
165		if err != nil {
166			return nil, err
167		}
168		if need > qvae.MaxStorageBufferBytes {
169			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: a %dx%d ceiling needs %d MB of VAE activations, "+
170				"past this device's %d MB single-buffer limit; the largest square is 1184x1184",
171				max.width, max.height, need>>20, qvae.MaxStorageBufferBytes>>20)
172		}
173	
174		set, err := safetensors.OpenSet(opt.Model + "/text_encoder")
175		if err != nil {
176			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: text encoder weights: %w", err)
177		}
178		if p.enc, err = qwen.NewGPUEncoder(dev, set, tcfg, tcfg.NumLayers, opt.MaxPrompt, nil); err != nil {
179			set.Close()
180			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: staging the text encoder: %w", err)
181		}
182		set.Close()
183	
184		// The DiT's row ceiling is the target's tokens plus the longest prompt:
185		// for t2i the prefix is the prompt and nothing else.
186		if p.dt, err = dit.NewGPU(dev, opt.Model+"/transformer", max.imgTokens+opt.MaxPrompt, opt.MaxPrompt); err != nil {
187			p.Destroy()
188			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: staging the transformer: %w", err)
189		}
190		if p.dec, err = qvae.NewGPUDecoder(dev, cpuDec, max.latentH, max.latentW); err != nil {
191			p.Destroy()
192			return nil, fmt.Errorf("pipeline: staging the VAE decoder: %w", err)
193		}
194	
195		p.encBytes = p.enc.WeightBytes()
196		p.vaeBytes = p.dec.WeightBytes()
197		p.ditBytes = p.dt.WeightBytes()
198		p.actBytes = p.enc.ActivationBytes() + p.dt.ActivationBytes() + p.dec.ActivationBytes()
199		return p, nil
200	}
201	
202	// Destroy releases the device residency.
203	func (p *Pipeline) Destroy() {
204		if p.dec != nil {
205			p.dec.Destroy()
206			p.dec = nil
207		}
208		if p.dt != nil {
209			p.dt.Destroy()
210			p.dt = nil
211		}
212		if p.enc != nil {
213			p.enc.Destroy()
214			p.enc = nil
215		}
216	}

102	// space, the same instrument TestEndToEndImage uses.
103	func imageDistance(got *zvae.Tensor, want *qwen.Mat) (maxAbs, mean float64) {
104		var sumAbs float64
105		for h := 0; h < got.H; h++ {
106			for w := 0; w < got.W; w++ {
107				for c := 0; c < got.C; c++ {
108					g := (float64(got.Plane(0, c)[h*got.W+w]) + 1) / 2
109					d := math.Abs(g - float64(want.Row(h*got.W + w)[c]))
110					if d > maxAbs {
111						maxAbs = d
112					}
113					sumAbs += d
114				}
115			}
116		}
117		return maxAbs, sumAbs / float64(got.C*got.H*got.W)

120	// The served path's bounds, in the two regimes the project's rule asks for
121	// (two-row-regime-needs-a-graph-gate, and Q4's own pair):
122	//
123	//   - teacherImgTol bounds the *composition*. Fed the oracle's own final
124	//     latents, everything downstream of the sampler is our decoder, and Q5g
125	//     measured that at max abs 7.3e-4 on this very case. 2.2e-2 is Z-Image's
126	//     end-to-end precedent and is kept as the bound so a regression here
127	//     reads against the same number the CPU gate does.
128	//   - servedImgTol bounds the *trajectory*. The served run is free-running
129	//     fp16: Q4 measured its latents drifting to rel 0.050 over 40 steps at
130	//     1024² against a 0.12 bound, and diffusers documents cache-on/off
131	//     producing visibly different but equally valid samples for the same
132	//     reason. So the image cannot be held to a fp32 tolerance, and what this
133	//     bound is for is catching a *break* — a wrong image is off by O(1) on
134	//     mean, not by hundredths.

137		servedImgTol  = 0.35

145	// latents through our decoder — bounds everything that is not the sampler,
146	// tightly. Free-running is the served path end to end, where fp16 through 36

163		final := loadRunMat(t, m, fmt.Sprintf("step%d_latents", m.Steps-1))

206	// matRel is the relative distance two latent matrices are apart, with an rms
207	// floor — pipeline_test.go's instrument, without the assertion.
208	func matRel(got, want *qwen.Mat) float64 {
209		var sumSq float64
210		for _, v := range want.Data {
211			sumSq += float64(v) * float64(v)
212		}
213		rms := math.Sqrt(sumSq / float64(len(want.Data)))
214		var rel float64
215		for i := range want.Data {
216			d := math.Abs(float64(got.Data[i]) - float64(want.Data[i]))
217			if r := d / math.Max(math.Abs(float64(want.Data[i])), math.Max(rms, 1e-12)); r > rel {
218				rel = r
219			}
220		}
221		return rel
222	}

---
(research/embedding-vertical.md E6). `-embed-tokens` sizes the arenas and is therefore where an
input is truncated: the front of the text survives and the end-of-text token
is re-appended, because last-token pooling takes *that* row and an input
truncated through it would be pooled from an ordinary word.

**The image pipeline is resident, and its resolution is not part of what is
resident.** `-image` stages 7.2 GB of text encoder, 12.5 GB of transformer and
0.3 GB of VAE in **21.2 s**, sizes 4.9 GB of activation arenas for
`-image-size`, and then a request moves no weight. That last clause is what
this endpoint needed and did not have: `zimage/pipeline` used to fix its width
and height at construction, so a size was a residency question.

one. The transformer states its run length per upload (`GPUStack.Upload`,

Every endpoint is *routed*, including the ones that are not implemented: a
client gets a 501 that says what is missing and, where a flag would have fixed
it, which flag. A 404 would mean a misspelled path and nothing else.

=== flags ===

    -embed         false          load Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    -embed-model   models/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B
    -embed-tokens  512            longest input the arenas hold; longer inputs are truncated

    -image             false               load Z-Image-Turbo
    -image-model       models/Z-Image-Turbo
    -image-size        1024x1024           the largest image the arenas hold, and the default
    -image-steps       8                   what a request that names no steps gets
    -image-max-prompt  512                 longest prompt the image text encoder is built for
    -preview           ""                  a madebyollin/taef1 checkpoint; loads the preview decoder
    -previews          false               shorthand for -preview models/taef1
    -edits             false               load the VAE's encoder, which is what lets /v1/images/edits answer

**-llm and -image do not fit together.** ~84 GB and ~25 GB against 128 GB of
unified memory the rest of the machine is also in: they are separate
processes on this part, or separate runs.

## A second turn is a continuation
=== 371 ===
reads as either 0.3 for the rest or one share before normalising and a mix
that guessed would still sound like a voice. An unknown name is a 400 naming
*which component* was unknown, since that is the one thing a three-part string
does not tell you. The `voices` array stays the list of single names: a blend
is every comma-joined subset of them and not a list anything could enumerate.

`POST /v1/images/generations` takes three fields that are not OpenAI's, and
each of them exists because the parameter is real here and there is nowhere
else to put it. **`"seed"`** names the initial latent's seed, and a response
reports the seed whether or not the request named one — a drawn seed that the
client is not told is an image that cannot be asked for twice. **`"steps"`**
is the denoising schedule's length, which is a host-side array and therefore
genuinely per request. And **`"aspect_ratio"`** — `"16:9"` and the like — is
fitted to the largest image *this* server holds, so a client wanting a
landscape picture does not have to know the ceiling to ask for one; `size`
wins when both are set, because that is the field every other server reads.
`GET /v1/models` carries an **`image`** object on the image model, alongside
the speech model's voices and for the same reason: `default_size`, `max_size`,
`size_multiple`, `default_steps`, `previews`, `max_partial_images`, `edits` and
`default_strength`, which are decided by what this process staged. The last
four are how a client finds out that `stream: true` and an edit will be
answered rather than discovering it from a 501.

**Streaming an image** is OpenAI's `stream` and `partial_images`, and it needs
`-preview`. The frames are `image_generation.partial_image` — `b64_json`,
`size`, `output_format` and `partial_image_index`, plus a `step`/`steps` pair
this server adds so a client watching one arrive knows how much is left —
followed by one `image_generation.completed` carrying the finished image and
the `seed` and `steps` that produced it. There is **no `[DONE]` sentinel**:
these events are named, so the terminal one is already unambiguous, and the
sentinel exists on the chat endpoint only because its frames are not.

Measured on one `-image -previews` process at 1024x1024, two runs each:

| request | wall clock | first picture |
|---|---|---|
| no stream | 14.72 s / 14.80 | 14.7 s |
| `stream: true` | 14.76 s / 14.75 | 14.8 s |
| `stream: true, partial_images: 3` | **15.40 s** / 15.41 | **3.6 s** |

So the framing is free and three in-progress frames cost **4.4%** — and what
they buy is a picture at 3.6 seconds instead of at fifteen. The frames land at
3.6, 7.1 and 10.7 s, from steps 1, 3 and 5 of the eight.

Two numbers inside that 4.4% are worth separating, because only one of them is
the model. A preview decode is **87 ms** (`madebyollin/taef1`, research/zimage-vertical.md I2);
encoding the frame is the other **60**, and it would have been **344** at Go's
default PNG compression — four times the decode. Partial frames therefore go
out at `png.BestSpeed`, 15% more bytes for a fifth of the latency, while the
finished image keeps the careful encoder. A transient frame and a deliverable
are not the same object.

**Which steps a partial comes from is the backend's decision**, not the
handler's: the step count may not have been named in the request, and how
finished a picture looks at step k is the scheduler's business. `backend`
spreads them evenly over *the steps that will actually run* and never takes
the last, whose denoised estimate *is* the final latent — a frame there would
be the finished image sent twice, once through each decoder. The "actually
run" is not pedantry: an edit at strength 0.5 runs the last four steps of
eight, and frames spread over all eight would every one of them fall before it
began.

### Editing a picture

`POST /v1/images/edits` needs `-image -edits`, and it takes **both encodings**:
`multipart/form-data`, which is what OpenAI's clients send and the only thing
their endpoint accepts, and a JSON body whose `image` is base64 (a `data:` URL
is fine), which is what curl and a test can write by hand. Both fill the same
struct.

**What it does is SDEdit** (research/zimage-vertical.md I7): the picture is encoded to a latent,
the latent is mixed with noise at an intermediate point on the schedule, and
only the tail of the schedule runs. **`strength`** is how far back up the
schedule that point is and is the whole behaviour of the endpoint — near zero
returns almost the picture that was sent, 1 discards it and is an ordinary
generation, and the default is 0.8. It is an extension because OpenAI has no
such field: their edit endpoint is an inpainting model driven by a mask, which
is a different mechanism.

Everything else is the generation endpoint's, including streaming, because
underneath an edit *is* a generation with a different starting latent. At

|---|---|---|

the model. A preview decode is **87 ms** (`madebyollin/taef1`, research/zimage-vertical.md I2);

finished image keeps the careful encoder. A transient frame and a deliverable

run" is not pedantry: an edit at strength 0.5 runs the last four steps of
eight, and frames spread over all eight would every one of them fall before it
began.

The port that owes it is IMAGE.md's Q8, and the large piece is the 27-layer
vision tower with its deepstack feature injection and 3-D mrope. The
endpoint's shape — both encodings, `multipart/form-data` for OpenAI's clients
and a JSON body whose `image` is base64 for curl — is unchanged and already
written; what is missing is underneath it.

**The size an edit with no `size` gets is the input picture's own shape**,
fitted inside the ceiling and rounded to a multiple of 16 — not the server's
default, which would silently reframe what was sent — and it is never scaled
*up*, because four times the tokens cannot paint detail the input never had. A
picture whose shape does not match the size being rendered is **cover-cropped**
rather than stretched, since an edit whose point is to keep the composition
should not begin by distorting it.

What is refused rather than faked:

- **`stream: true` on speech.** Kokoro decides the whole utterance's durations
  before a single sample exists, so there is nothing to send early. A whole
  body dressed as a stream would be a lie about latency.
- **`stream: true` on transcription.** The decode loop emits token by token
  and could stream, but the 40 µs submit-and-fence per emission is 38% of it
  (research/speech-vertical.md), so what that endpoint wants is the persistent kernel, not a
  goroutine.
- **Containers other than WAV, and audio formats other than wav/pcm.**
  `audio/` is 16-bit PCM in and out on purpose. An mp3 request gets a 400
  naming what the server does encode. *Transcripts* are a different question
  and are no longer refused: `json`, `verbose_json`, `text`, `srt` and `vtt`
  all answer, because the timings they need exist.
- **`stream: true` without `-preview`.** It is a 501 naming the flag rather
  than a 400, because the request is well formed and the server was started
  without the decoder that answers it. With the flag it streams; see above.
  `/v1/images/edits` without `-edits` is the same answer about the encoder.
- **A `mask` on an edit.** A 501 that says what it would be rather than a

91	### The four mechanisms that make it different from Z-Image
92	
93	**1. One joint sequence, block-causal.** Text embeddings and image latents
94	share a single stream. The mask is `(q_idx >= kv_idx) OR same_image_block`:
95	the sequence is causal, text tokens strictly so, but every image block (each
96	condition image, and the target) is internally bidirectional. In diffusers the
97	non-flex processor decomposes this exactly into one attention call per prefix
98	segment (text segments get a causal triangle) plus one full-attention call for
99	the target — that decomposition, not a masked kernel, is the shape we port.

102	are modulated from **t = 0** (the modulation tensor carries batch+1 rows; the
103	target's tokens read their sample's row, everything else reads the t=0 row).
104	That makes the prefix's activations step-independent, so **step 0 runs the
105	full block-causal prefill and stores per-layer post-RoPE K/V for the prefix;
106	steps 1..N-1 recompute only the target's tokens**, attending over
107	[cached prefix K/V ++ fresh target K/V] with no mask at all (batch 1, no
108	padding). For t2i the prefix is just the prompt (tens of tokens — small win);
109	for edits it is thousands of tokens per reference image (large win). Caching
110	on/off changes rounding, not correctness — diffusers documents that the two
111	settings give *visibly different but equally valid* samples. **We ship
112	cache-on and validate against diffusers `use_kv_cache=True`.**

**Open, in order of what a round trip buys:**

- **The generator's 12 ms and the tail's 8** — the only arithmetic-bound
  parts of the model, 65% of a short utterance, measured since T4.
- **The host embedding stack** (R1's #2): `bert` is 12 ms of a paragraph
  and only 2.5 on the device — the "not worth a dispatch" comment is stale
  the same way the attention kernel's was.
- **Three boundaries, one change each**: the excitation's 0.2 ms is 88%
  submit+readback (move the two noise convolutions onto the device and
  nothing of that stage touches the bus); the phoneme side's remaining 6 ms
  is readbacks and submits (move the vocoder's input boundary); a 16 kHz
  path out of the vocoder would delete the client resample (9.7% of the
  loop — can the iSTFT head be asked for the rate directly?).
- **G2P on unseen text**: designed corpus 24/24; on 400 unseen sentences
  68.8% of sentences, 92.4% of phoneme words agree with misaki. Closing the
  gap is more *measured* rules — the syntactically obvious ones scored
  worse than no tagger.
- **Known, unsettled**: the style row is indexed by the phoneme *character*
  count (upstream's behaviour), so a front end emitting different characters
  picks a different row. And kokoro spells numbers out where parakeet writes
  digits back — the round trip measures those three cases and does not
  count them as failures.

## Image generation (archive: [`research/zimage-vertical.md`](research/zimage-vertical.md), slice: [`research/zimage-pipeline.md`](research/zimage-pipeline.md))

**Where it stands.** The slice (stages 1–10) hit 14.26 s an image; serving
work closed 2026-09-18: variable geometry under a ceiling (I1), taef1
previews with `stream: true` (I2 — three partials cost 4.4% and put a
picture at 3.6 s), and `/v1/images/edits` over SDEdit with the ported VAE
encoder (I7 — an edit is cheaper than a generation by exactly the steps it
skips). Reproduces diffusers to 2.2e-2; every capability `GOALS.md` names
is served. Kernel work parked; the order was capabilities before percents,
and the capabilities ran out.

**Open (all percents):**

- **I3 + I5 + I8 + I9 — the same fusion in four places, 1.9 s of 14.3**: a

is the honest fast setting** at −35% with no visible loss on any of them,

**Q6 is done — the image vertical is served on Qwen-Image-2.1.**

## The headline

`POST /v1/images/generations` answers from a 31.7 GB resident pipeline. **1024²/40 steps: 1m38.2s / 1m41.3s** (two runs), staged in 28 s. By stage: text encoder 107 ms, DiT prefill 2.28 s, 39 cached steps mean 2.26 s, VAE decode 7.5 s — **92% of an image is the denoising steps**, 7.6% the VAE, 0.1% the text encoder.

## What I built

- **`qimage/pipeline.Pipeline`** — the resident three-model graph. Everything between the models is host arithmetic per request, so a size is a parameter and only the ceiling is residency.
- **`backend/image.go`** re-wired onto it; **`cmd/serve -image`**; **`cmd/qimage`** (cmd/zimage's replacement).
- **`background: "transparent"`** through `api` — new field, validated, plumbed. It works: the dragon sticker above is the same prompt/seed opaque vs transparent, the right one shown over red to prove the alpha is real. Z-Image couldn't do this at all.

## Gates

`TestServedOracle256`, both regimes. Teacher-forced: **max abs 2.0e-5**. Free-running — the served path exactly, fp16 through 36 encoder layers and 32 DiT blocks — **max abs 0.0333, mean 3.4e-4** from the fp32 reference, which is 1.5x Z-Image's *fp32* precedent on a path that narrows everything. The 1024² eyeball Q4 deferred is a photorealistic fox.

I also drove the real server over HTTP: `/v1/models` reports the geometry, 512²/24 comes back in 16.8 s then 14.5 s, and every refusal path returns the right code.

## Two findings worth the space

**The step sweep's answer is the prompt, not the count.** Photographic and painterly prompts are convincing at **12 steps** (36 s, a third of the cost). The bicycle-drivetrain diagram is good at 24 and has *disintegrated* by 12 — floating parts, contrast collapsing. So 40 stays the default as the only count safe across prompt kinds, with 24 documented as the honest fast setting. The pixel distances the sweep also reports are not the judgement, and the test says so — fewer steps integrate a different trajectory, not a worse one.

**Two capabilities regressed with the model swap**, and I made both refuse with the stage that owes them rather than a flag that no longer exists: `stream: true` (Q7 — no tiny decoder for this VAE) and `/v1/images/edits` (Q8 — 2.1 edits by conditional generation over an unported vision tower). `-preview`/`-previews`/`-edits` are now immediate startup errors. I had to fix two stale refusal messages I found only by driving the live server — they were still telling clients to pass `-preview models/taef1`.

## What I deliberately did *not* do

**Deleted** (25 files): `zimage/dit`, `zimage/pipeline`, `cmd/zimage`, `cmd/ditstack`, `cmd/ditbench`, `cmd/ditblock`.

**Kept `zimage/vae`**, against IMAGE.md's "delete as each stage lands". Its `gpu_conv.go` is the validated test bed for the one kernel Q9 wants — `TestGPUConvMatchesScalar` proves the matrix-core convolution against a scalar oracle, and deleting it now would throw away the proof and keep the problem. It goes when Q9 has taken the packing helpers across; IMAGE.md now says so.

**Did not delete the 62 GB of Z-Image weights.** Nothing reads them, so it's one `rm -rf models/Z-Image-Turbo models/taef1` whenever you want the space — but that's not cheaply reversible and isn't mine to do unasked.

Full suite green: `api`, `backend`, `qimage/...`, `zimage/...`. IMAGE.md, TODO.md and API.md updated with the measurements; Q-o1 closed.

content.content:
## The preview problem (taef1 has no successor here)

`madebyollin/taehv`'s **taew2_1 does *not* fit this model**: it decodes the
Wan-2.1 16-channel/8x latent that the *original* Qwen-Image borrowed; 2.1's
VAE is a new 64-channel/16x RGBA design, and as of today taehv lists nothing
for it. So, in order:

1. **Q7 ships a fitted linear preview**: a 64→3 (or →4) matrix, least-squares
   over dumped (latent, 1/16-scale image) pairs — the latent2rgb approach.
   One GEMV per pixel, effectively free per step; a 1024² generation previews
   at 64x64, upscaled client-side. Fitting data comes out of Q0's dumps.
2. **Watch taehv** for a 2.1 variant and port it like `zimage/vae/tiny.go`
   (at T=1 its temporal machinery degenerates; it would be a small 2D conv
   stack again). Do not build our own distilled decoder — that is a training
   project this repo does not want.

## What survives, what is new, what dies
=== Q7 stage ===
497:- **Q7 — previews.** Fit the linear 64→RGB matrix from Q0's pairs, wire
498-  `stream: true`/`partial_images` back up.
499-- **Q8 — edits.** The big one, in three parts: (a) VAE encoder serving
500-  reference latents (Q5 built it), (b) **the vision tower** — 27-layer ViT,
501-  2x2 spatial merge, interpolated position grid, deepstack feature injection

3	// (IMAGE.md Q7).
4	//
5	//	go run ./cmd/previewfit -out qimage/pipeline/preview_matrix.go
6	//	go run ./cmd/previewfit -size 512 -steps 8 -report   # refit and score it
7	//
8	// **It generates its own training data rather than reading a dump**, which
9	// is the one judgement in here. Q0's dumps carry two (latent, image) pairs;
10	// this runs the served pipeline over a prompt set chosen to span colour and
11	// content, and every pair it collects is a latent this decoder decoded into
12	// that image -- the two sides cannot disagree about normalisation, layout or
13	// range, which is exactly the class of mistake a hand-assembled pair set
14	// invites.
15	//
16	// The fit itself is ordinary least squares on the normal equations: one
17	// 65x65 system (64 latent channels plus a bias) with four right-hand sides,
18	// solved in float64 by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. At that
19	// size nothing about conditioning is interesting, and the residual it
20	// reports is what says whether the model is adequate -- a linear map of a
21	// 64-channel latent cannot represent a convolutional decoder, and the number
22	// to read is how much of the colour it does get.
23	package main
24	
25	import (
26		"flag"
27		"fmt"
28		"log"
29		"math"
30		"os"
31		"strings"
32		"time"
33	
34		"strix-halo-vulkan/qimage/pipeline"
35		"strix-halo-vulkan/vk"
36		"strix-halo-vulkan/zimage/qwen"
37		zvae "strix-halo-vulkan/zimage/vae"
38	)
39	
40	const strixHaloDeviceID = 0x1586
41	
42	// fitPrompts span what the matrix has to get right: saturated primaries,
43	// skin and foliage, night and snow, flat graphic colour and neutral greys.
44	// A latent2rgb matrix that saw only photographs of one palette maps
45	// everything else toward it, and the failure is invisible in the fit's own
46	// residual.
47	var fitPrompts = []string{
48		"a red fox sitting in fresh snow at dawn, photograph",
49		"an oil painting of a harbour at sunset, thick impasto brushwork",
50		"a bowl of lemons and limes on a blue tablecloth, still life photograph",
51		"a dense green rainforest canopy seen from above, aerial photograph",
52		"a portrait of an elderly woman with grey hair, soft window light",
53		"a neon-lit city street at night in the rain, cinematic",
54		"a white ceramic teapot on a white table, high key studio lighting",
55		"a black cat asleep on a dark sofa, low key photograph",
56		"a flat vector illustration of a mountain range, bold orange and teal",
57		"a close-up of rusted iron and peeling blue paint, texture photograph",
58		"a field of purple lavender under a stormy grey sky",
59		"a bright yellow taxi on a wet asphalt road, shallow depth of field",
60		"an underwater photograph of a coral reef, turquoise water",
61		"a slice of chocolate cake on a pink plate, food photography",
62		"a snowy mountain peak against a deep blue sky, clear day",
63		"a crowded market stall of colourful spices, warm light",
64		"a single white daisy on a black background, macro photograph",
65		"a desert dune landscape at midday, pale sand and hard shadows",
66		"a stack of old books and a brass lamp, sepia tones",
67		"a cartoon sticker of a smiling green frog, flat colour",
68		"a stormy grey sea with white foam, long exposure",
69		"a bright red London bus on a grey street",
70		"a bunch of ripe bananas on a wooden board",
71		"an abstract pastel gradient of pink and mint, smooth",
72	}
73	
74	func main() {
75		log.SetFlags(0)
76		model := flag.String("model", "models/Qwen-Image-2.1", "checkpoint root")
77		out := flag.String("out", "", "write the Go source here; empty prints it")
78		size := flag.Int("size", 512, "fitting resolution; each image gives (size/16)^2 samples")
79		steps := flag.Int("steps", 8, "denoising steps per fitting image; the picture only has to be a picture")
80		seed := flag.Int64("seed", 20260920, "base seed")
81		report := flag.Bool("report", false, "also score the fit against a held-out tail of the prompt set")
82		flag.Parse()
83	
84		inst, err := vk.NewInstance("previewfit")
85		must(err)
86		defer inst.Destroy()
87		devs, err := inst.PhysicalDevices()
88		must(err)
89		phys := &devs[0]
90		for i := range devs {
91			if devs[i].DeviceID == strixHaloDeviceID {
92				phys = &devs[i]
93			}
94		}
95		qf, err := phys.ComputeQueueFamily()
96		must(err)
97		sgs, err := phys.SubgroupSizeControl()
98		must(err)
99		dev, err := vk.NewDevice(phys, qf, vk.DeviceFeatures{
100			Float16: true, CoopMatrix: true, SubgroupSizeControl: sgs.Supported,
101		})
102		must(err)
103		defer dev.Destroy()
104	
105		p, err := pipeline.New(dev, pipeline.Options{
106			Model: *model, Width: *size, Height: *size, Steps: *steps,
107		})
108		must(err)
109		defer p.Destroy()
110	
111		side := *size / 16
112		// Held out: the last quarter of the prompt set never enters the normal
113		// equations, so -report's number is a generalisation error rather than a
114		// residual. A 260-parameter model over 6000 samples would not overfit,
115		// but "would not" is not a measurement.
116		hold := len(fitPrompts)
117		if *report {
118			hold = len(fitPrompts) * 3 / 4
119		}
120	
121		var train, test []sample
122		start := time.Now()
123		for i, prompt := range fitPrompts {
124			latents, img, err := renderPair(p, prompt, *seed+int64(i), *size, *steps)
125			must(err)
126			s := pairSamples(latents, img, side)
127			if i < hold {
128				train = append(train, s...)
129			} else {
130				test = append(test, s...)
131			}
132			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "  [%2d/%d] %-52s %d samples\n", i+1, len(fitPrompts), truncate(prompt, 52), len(s))
133		}
134		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "collected %d training samples (%d held out) in %v\n",
135			len(train), len(test), time.Since(start).Round(time.Second))
136	
137		w, b := fit(train)
138		reportFit(os.Stderr, "train", train, w, b)
139		if len(test) > 0 {

141		}
142	
143		src := render(w, b)
144		if *out == "" {

146			return
147		}
148		must(os.WriteFile(*out, []byte(src), 0o644))
149		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "wrote %s\n", *out)
150	}

152	// sample is one latent pixel and the average colour of the 16x16 image block
153	// it produced.
154	type sample struct {
155		z   []float32
156		rgb [4]float64

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='API.md'
s=open(p).read()
start = s.index("**Streaming an image is refused for now**")
end = s.index("### Editing a picture")
new = '''**Streaming an image** is OpenAI's `stream` and `partial_images`. The frames
are `image_generation.partial_image` — `b64_json`, `size`, `output_format`
and `partial_image_index`, plus a `step`/`steps` pair this server adds so a
client watching one arrive knows how much is left — followed by one
`image_generation.completed` carrying the finished image and the `seed` and
`steps` that produced it. There is **no `[DONE]` sentinel**: these events are
named, so the terminal one is already unambiguous, and the sentinel exists on
the chat endpoint only because its frames are not.

**It needs no flag, and that is the change from Z-Image-Turbo rather than an
omission.** There, previewing meant loading `madebyollin/taef1` beside the
full VAE — 1.0 GB of activation arena, so streaming was a residency decision
and `-preview` was how you made it. Qwen-Image-2.1's 64-channel VAE has no
distilled decoder in existence, so the preview here is a **fitted linear
64→RGBA matrix**: 260 float32s compiled into the binary, least-squares
fitted against the real decoder's own output (IMAGE.md Q7, R² 0.97 on RGB).
There is nothing to load and nothing to turn on.

Measured on one `-image -image-size 512x512 -image-steps 16` process, two
runs each:

| request | wall clock | first picture |
|---|---|---|
| no stream | 10.25 s / 10.23 | 10.3 s |
| `stream: true` | 10.26 s / 10.28 | 10.3 s |
| `stream: true, partial_images: 3` | **10.27 s** / 10.28 | **2.27 s** |

So the framing is free and three in-progress frames cost **0.3%** — against
4.4% through taef1 — and what they buy is a picture at 2.3 seconds instead
of at ten. The frames land at 2.27, 4.34 and 6.43 s, from steps 3, 7 and 11
of the sixteen.

A preview decode itself is **159 µs** against a 587 ms step; everything else
in that 0.3% is encoding the PNG and writing it. Partial frames go out at
`png.BestSpeed` — 15% more bytes for a fifth of the latency — while the
finished image keeps the careful encoder. A transient frame and a deliverable
are not the same object. **A frame is 1/16 scale** (32x32 for a 512x512
image, 64x64 for a 1024x1024 one) and is upscaled by whatever displays it: a
latent2rgb map carries composition, colour and layout, and cannot carry
texture the latent does not hold per-pixel.

**What the frame decodes is the denoised estimate, not the current latent**,
and the distinction is load-bearing. The schedule is flow matching, so the
sample at step k is an interpolation x_t = (1−σ)·x0 + σ·ε — ten steps into
forty it is still three quarters noise, and mapping *that* through any
decoder gives a picture of noise. The estimate x0 = x_t − σ·v is what looks
like the image, and the loop forms it for nothing because it has the
velocity in hand.

**Which steps a partial comes from is the backend's decision**, not the
handler's: the step count may not have been named in the request, and how
finished a picture looks at step k is the scheduler's business. `backend`
spreads them evenly over the steps that will actually run and never takes the
last, whose denoised estimate *is* the final latent — a frame there would be
the finished image sent twice, once through each decoder.

'''
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)

content.text:
**Q7 is done — in-progress previews are back, and cheaper than they were under Z-Image.**

## The decoder

No tiny autoencoder exists for this VAE (taehv's taew2_1 decodes a different latent entirely), so the preview is the latent2rgb trick: **one 64×4 matrix and a bias, 260 float32s compiled in**. `cmd/previewfit` generates its own training pairs rather than reading Q0's two — it runs the served pipeline over 24 prompts chosen to span colour and content, box-filters each 16×16 image block onto the latent pixel that produced it, and solves one 65×65 normal system. A pair the pipeline produced itself can't disagree with it about normalisation or layout.

**Fit quality, both numbers.** The shipped matrix scores R² 0.969–0.974 on RGB. But `-report` holds the last six prompts out entirely and gives **R² 0.83–0.90 on unseen content** — that's the honest one, and the gap is real: six held-out prompts are six palettes it never saw. Right order for something whose job is composition and colour, not fidelity.

## The cost, which changed the design

A preview decode is **159 µs against a 587 ms step**. Over HTTP, three partials cost **0.3%** of a request (10.27 s vs 10.24 at 512²/16) — against 4.4% through taef1 — and put the first picture at **2.27 s instead of 10.25**.

So I deleted `-preview` and `-previews` rather than repurposing them. Under Z-Image they bought 1.0 GB of activation arena and streaming was a residency decision; here there is nothing to load, and a flag that can't be turned off isn't a flag. `previews: true` is now unconditional in `/v1/models`.

## The mechanism worth pinning

**The frame decodes the denoised estimate x0, not the sample.** Flow matching means the sample ten steps into forty is still three quarters noise — mapping *that* through any decoder gives noise. `Run` forms x0 after the Euler move, where the identity is `x0 = x_{t+1} − σ_next·v` and no copy of the pre-step latents is needed.

`TestPreviewFrames` carries that as a **negative control**: decoding the sample instead is 2.5× further from the finished image at step 0 (0.394 vs 0.157), and the two are asserted *identical* at the last step, where the terminal sigma makes them the same quantity.

## One thing I had to go back and fix

The api's "no preview decoder" refusal — which I'd rewritten an hour earlier to say the matrix "is not built (IMAGE.md Q7)" — became false the moment I built it. It's now generic and points at `image.previews` in `/v1/models`, since the shipped backend always has previews and that branch only fires for a backend that reports otherwise. Its test changed with it.

Full suite green (`api`, `backend`, `qimage/...`, `zimage/...`), vet clean. IMAGE.md, API.md and TODO.md updated; Q7 marked done with the measurements. **Q8 (edits) is now the only regression left from the model swap.**

        self,
        prompt: str | list[str] = None,
        image: list | None = None,
        device: torch.device | None = None,

            prompts = [self.prompt_template_t2i.format(t) for t in prompt]

            prompts = []
            condition_pil_list = []
            for t in prompt:
                n_imgs = len(image)
                replace = "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>"
                for i in range(2, n_imgs + 1):
                    replace += f" <image{i}><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>"
                template = self.prompt_template_ti2i.replace(
                    "<image1><|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>", replace

                prompts.append(template.format(t))
            # Each prompt's template repeats the `<|image_pad|>` placeholders, so hand the processor one set of
            # images per prompt, in the order the placeholders appear.
            for _ in prompt:
                for img in image:
                    if not isinstance(img, PILImage.Image):
                        img = PILImage.fromarray(img)
                    if img.mode == "RGBA":
                        # The checkpoint was trained with the alpha composited over white for the vision encoder.
                        # Only this copy is flattened; the VAE still reads all four channels.
                        white = PILImage.new("RGB", img.size, (255, 255, 255))

        processor_kwargs = {
            "text": prompts,
            "padding": True,
            "padding_side": "left",
            "return_tensors": "pt",

            processor_kwargs["images"] = condition_pil_list

            "input_ids": model_inputs.input_ids,
            "attention_mask": model_inputs.attention_mask,
            "output_hidden_states": True,

            forward_kwargs.update(pixel_values=model_inputs.pixel_values, image_grid_thw=model_inputs.image_grid_thw)

        )

            [torch.cat([u, u.new_zeros(max_seq_len - u.size(0))]) for u in attn_mask_list]
        )
        image_pad_mask = torch.stack([torch.cat([u, u.new_zeros(max_seq_len - u.size(0))]) for u in image_pad_mask])

    def dump(name, t):

            "sum": float(flat.double().sum()), "absmax": float(flat.abs().max()),
        }
        print(f"  {name:24s} {str(list(t.shape)):18s} sum={flat.double().sum():+.5f} absmax={flat.abs().max():.4g}")

    for label, prompt in PROMPTS.items():
        # --- the pipeline's own path: what the DiT is fed -------------------
        with torch.no_grad():
            embeds, mask, pad_mask = pipe._get_qwen_prompt_embeds(prompt, None, device="cpu")
        rendered = pipe.prompt_template_t2i.format(prompt if prompt else " ")
        ids = proc(text=[rendered], return_tensors="pt").input_ids
        manifest["prompts"][label] = {
            "prompt": prompt, "rendered": rendered, "ids": ids[0].tolist(),
            "seq": ids.shape[1], "embed_tokens": embeds.shape[1],
        }
        print(f"{label}: {ids.shape[1]} tokens, {embeds.shape[1]} after drop")
        dump(label + "_prompt_embeds", embeds)
        dump(label + "_ids", ids.to(torch.float32))

        # --- the layer walk: every decoder layer's output -------------------
        if label == "en":
            text_model = getattr(te.model, "language_model", te.model)
            captured = {}
            rope_handle = text_model.rotary_emb.register_forward_hook(
                lambda m, a, out: captured.update(cos=out[0], sin=out[1])
            )
            norm_handle = text_model.norm.register_forward_hook(lambda m, a, out: a[0])
            with torch.no_grad():
                outputs = te(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=torch.ones_like(ids), output_hidden_states=True)
            rope_handle.remove()
            norm_handle.remove()
            hs = outputs.hidden_states
            dump("en_embed_tokens", hs[0])
            for i in (WALK_LAYER, WALK_LAYER + 1):
                dump(f"en_layer{i}_out", hs[i + 1])
            dump("en_last_prenorm", hs[-1])

            # hidden_states[-1] with the hook == the pipeline's pre-drop rows
            gap = (hs[-1][:, pipe._drop_idx:] - embeds).abs().max()
            manifest["prompts"]["en"]["prenorm_vs_pipeline_gap"] = float(gap)

            # --- Q-o5: text-only mrope against a plain NeoX table ----------
            cos, sin = captured["cos"], captured["sin"]
            T, hd = ids.shape[1], tcfg.head_dim
            theta = float(tcfg.rope_parameters["rope_theta"])
            inv = 1.0 / theta ** (torch.arange(0, hd, 2, dtype=torch.float32) / hd)
            ang = torch.arange(T, dtype=torch.float32)[:, None] * inv[None]
            plain_cos = torch.cat([ang.cos(), ang.cos()], dim=-1)
            plain_sin = torch.cat([ang.sin(), ang.sin()], dim=-1)
            mrope_gap = max(
                float((cos.reshape(T, hd) - plain_cos).abs().max()),
                float((sin.reshape(T, hd) - plain_sin).abs().max()),
            )
            manifest["mrope_gap"] = mrope_gap
            manifest["rope_shapes"] = {"cos": list(cos.shape), "sin": list(sin.shape)}
            dump("en_rope_cos", cos.reshape(T, hd) if cos.numel() == T * hd else cos)
            dump("en_rope_sin", sin.reshape(T, hd) if sin.numel() == T * hd else sin)
            print(f"  prenorm-vs-pipeline gap {gap:.3g}; mrope-vs-plain-rope gap {mrope_gap:.3g}")

    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "manifest.json"), "w") as fh:
        json.dump(manifest, fh, indent=2)
    print(f"wrote {len(manifest['tensors'])} tensors to {OUT}")

the Go pipeline's image is compared against.

The whole pipeline in fp32 on CPU (~65 GB RSS), 256x256 in 4 steps — small on
purpose: this is the parity oracle, not a quality sample. `use_kv_cache=True`
because that is the shipped configuration (IMAGE.md decision 2); the cache-off
sample is a *different valid image* by design, so there is exactly one oracle.

The initial noise is generated here and passed in packed, so the Go side gets
the noise as data rather than having to reproduce torch's RNG. Dumped: the
prompt embeddings, the packed noise, the latents after every step, the final
latent, the RGBA image tensor, and a PNG for the eyeball.

manifests: CPU fp32 is deterministic, the sums must match exactly.

The one-time full-size oracle (~1 h CPU, ~65 GB RSS; holds ~half the machine,
so not while an LLM whole-model run is up):

    .venv/bin/python reference/dump_qi21_run.py --size 1024 --steps 40 --out reference/out/qi21run1024

input.content:
"""Dump Qwen-Image-2.1's vision tower and its image-conditioned text
encoding, for Q8 — the oracle the Go port of an *edit's* prefix is gated
against.

Everything an edit adds over a generation is on this path and nowhere else.
Q2 already validated the DiT's edit case (per-reference RoPE blocks, the
segments, the prefix cache) against `out/qi21dit` and `out/qi21block`, and
Q5 the VAE encoder that supplies the reference latents. What has never been
run in Go is the other half of a condition image: the 27-layer ViT that
turns its pixels into vision context, the three deepstack taps that are
injected into the text model's first layers, and the 3-D mrope the text
model uses once real image positions exist.

So this walks all of it, stage by stage:

  * the processor's patching — `pixel_values` is [patches, 1536] where 1536
    is 3 channels x 2 temporal x 16 x 16, and the temporal axis is the same
    frame twice. The Go side has to reproduce that layout exactly, so it is
    dumped rather than described;
  * the tower's *interpolated* position embedding. The checkpoint holds 2304
    = 48x48 learned positions and any image grid is a bilinear resample of
    them, which is four (index, weight) pairs per patch — dumped as the
    indices and weights the model itself computed, because reproducing the
    resample is the single most mistakable piece here;
  * the vision rotary table, every block's output, the three deepstack
    features (layers 8/16/24) and the 2x2 patch merger;
  * the text side: the 3-D mrope position ids for a sequence that contains
    image tokens, the input embeddings *after* the merger's output has been
    scattered into the `<|image_pad|>` slots, and the pipeline's own
    `prompt_embeds` and `image_pad_mask`.

A fact this dump exists to pin, and the one Q8 rests on: the DiT overwrites
the image-slot rows with VAE latents, so vision content reaches it **only
through what the text tokens absorbed inside the encoder's attention**. The
tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels. `edit_merged_rows`
and `edit_prompt_embeds` are the two sides of that.

The condition image is generated here — a deterministic 256x256 RGBA card —
so the dump needs no asset and two runs are byte-identical.

    .venv/bin/python reference/dump_qi21_vision.py   (~36 GB RSS, minutes)

The end-to-end edit oracle is a separate, heavier script: the full pipeline
in fp32 is ~68 GB and must run alone.
"""

import json
import os

import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoModel, Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration, Qwen3VLProcessor

OUT = "reference/out/qi21vision"
MODEL = "models/Qwen-Image-2.1"
PROMPT = "make the sky a deep orange sunset"
# 256x256 is the processor's own minimum (shortest_edge is 65536 pixels), so
# the card passes through unresized: the grid is 16x16 patches, 64 image-pad
# slots, and every stage below stays small enough to read.
SIZE = 256


def test_card(size):
    """A deterministic RGBA card: colour ramps, hard edges and a gradient
    alpha, so the tower sees structure at every frequency it could care
    about. Same idea as dump_qi21_vae.py's card, at the tower's size."""
    y, x = np.mgrid[0:size, 0:size].astype(np.float64) / (size - 1)
    r = np.where((x * 4).astype(int) % 2 == 0, x, 1 - y)
    g = np.sin(6.0 * np.pi * y) * 0.5 + 0.5
    b = np.where(((x * 8).astype(int) + (y * 8).astype(int)) % 2 == 0, 0.15, 0.85)
    a = np.clip(0.25 + 0.75 * x, 0, 1)
    card = np.stack([r, g, b, a], axis=-1)
    return (card * 255).round().astype(np.uint8)


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    proc = Qwen3VLProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL, subfolder="processor")
    te = Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
        MODEL, subfolder="text_encoder", dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="eager"
    ).eval()
    pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline(
        scheduler=None, vae=None, text_encoder=te, processor=proc, transformer=None
    )

    vcfg = te.config.vision_config
    tcfg = te.config.text_config
    manifest = {
        "template_ti2i": pipe.prompt_template_ti2i,
        "drop_idx": pipe._drop_idx,
        "image_token_id": pipe._img_token_id,
        "prompt": PROMPT,
        "size": SIZE,
        "vision": {
            "depth": vcfg.depth, "hidden_size": vcfg.hidden_size,
            "num_heads": vcfg.num_heads, "head_dim": vcfg.hidden_size // vcfg.num_heads,
            "intermediate_size": vcfg.intermediate_size, "hidden_act": vcfg.hidden_act,
            "patch_size": vcfg.patch_size, "spatial_merge_size": vcfg.spatial_merge_size,
            "temporal_patch_size": vcfg.temporal_patch_size,
            "in_channels": vcfg.in_channels,
            "num_position_embeddings": vcfg.num_position_embeddings,
            "out_hidden_size": vcfg.out_hidden_size,
            "deepstack_visual_indexes": list(vcfg.deepstack_visual_indexes),
        },
        "text": {
            "mrope_section": tcfg.rope_parameters.get("mrope_section"),
            "mrope_interleaved": tcfg.rope_parameters.get("mrope_interleaved"),
            "rope_theta": tcfg.rope_parameters["rope_theta"],
            "head_dim": tcfg.head_dim,
        },
        "tensors": {},
    }

    def dump(name, t):
        t = t.detach().contiguous().to(torch.float32)
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, name + ".bin"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(t.numpy().tobytes())
        flat = t.flatten()
        manifest["tensors"][name] = {
            "shape": list(t.shape), "count": int(flat.numel()),
            "sum": float(flat.double().sum()), "absmax": float(flat.abs().max()),
        }
        print(f"  {name:26s} {str(list(t.shape)):20s} sum={flat.double().sum():+.5f} absmax={flat.abs().max():.4g}")

    # --- the condition image, both copies -------------------------------
    #
    # The pipeline flattens alpha over white for the *vision* copy only and
    # feeds all four channels to the VAE. Both are dumped, because a port
    # that flattens once and uses it twice is a bug this pins.
    card = test_card(SIZE)
    rgba = Image.fromarray(card, mode="RGBA")
    white = Image.new("RGB", rgba.size, (255, 255, 255))
    white.paste(rgba, mask=rgba.getchannel("A"))
    dump("card_rgba", torch.from_numpy(card).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)
    dump("card_vision_rgb", torch.from_numpy(np.array(white)).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)

    # --- what the processor produces ------------------------------------
    rendered = pipe.prompt_template_ti2i.format(PROMPT)
    inputs = proc(text=[rendered], images=[white], padding=True, padding_side="left", return_tensors="pt")
    ids = inputs.input_ids
    grid = inputs.image_grid_thw
    manifest["rendered"] = rendered
    manifest["ids"] = ids[0].tolist()
    manifest["grid_thw"] = grid.tolist()
    manifest["seq"] = int(ids.shape[1])
    manifest["image_pad_positions"] = [i for i, v in enumerate(ids[0].tolist()) if v == pipe._img_token_id]
    print(f"{ids.shape[1]} tokens, grid {grid.tolist()}, "
          f"{len(manifest['image_pad_positions'])} image-pad slots, drop_idx {pipe._drop_idx}")
    dump("pixel_values", inputs.pixel_values)
    dump("ids", ids.float())

    # --- the vision tower, stage by stage -------------------------------
    visual = te.model.visual
    caps = {}
    handles = [

"""Dump Qwen-Image-2.1's vision tower and its image-conditioned text
encoding, for Q8 — the oracle the Go port of an *edit's* prefix is gated
against.

Everything an edit adds over a generation is on this path and nowhere else.
Q2 already validated the DiT's edit case (per-reference RoPE blocks, the
segments, the prefix cache) against `out/qi21dit` and `out/qi21block`, and
Q5 the VAE encoder that supplies the reference latents. What has never been
run in Go is the other half of a condition image: the 27-layer ViT that
turns its pixels into vision context, the three deepstack taps that are
injected into the text model's first layers, and the 3-D mrope the text
model uses once real image positions exist.

So this walks all of it, stage by stage:

  * the processor's patching — `pixel_values` is [patches, 1536] where 1536
    is 3 channels x 2 temporal x 16 x 16, and the temporal axis is the same
    frame twice. The Go side has to reproduce that layout exactly, so it is
    dumped rather than described;
  * the tower's *interpolated* position embedding. The checkpoint holds 2304
    = 48x48 learned positions and any image grid is a bilinear resample of
    them, which is four (index, weight) pairs per patch — dumped as the
    indices and weights the model itself computed, because reproducing the
    resample is the single most mistakable piece here;
  * the vision rotary table, every block's output, the three deepstack
    features (layers 8/16/24) and the 2x2 patch merger;
  * the text side: the 3-D mrope position ids for a sequence that contains
    image tokens, the input embeddings *after* the merger's output has been
    scattered into the `<|image_pad|>` slots, and the pipeline's own
    `prompt_embeds` and `image_pad_mask`.

A fact this dump exists to pin, and the one Q8 rests on: the DiT overwrites
the image-slot rows with VAE latents, so vision content reaches it **only
through what the text tokens absorbed inside the encoder's attention**. The
tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels. `edit_merged_rows`
and `edit_prompt_embeds` are the two sides of that.

The condition image is generated here — a deterministic 256x256 RGBA card —
so the dump needs no asset and two runs are byte-identical.

    .venv/bin/python reference/dump_qi21_vision.py   (~36 GB RSS, minutes)

The end-to-end edit oracle is a separate, heavier script: the full pipeline
in fp32 is ~68 GB and must run alone.

import os

import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline

# the card passes through unresized: the grid is 16x16 patches, 64 image-pad
# slots, and every stage below stays small enough to read.

    """A deterministic RGBA card: colour ramps, hard edges and a gradient
    alpha, so the tower sees structure at every frequency it could care
    about. Same idea as dump_qi21_vae.py's card, at the tower's size."""
    y, x = np.mgrid[0:size, 0:size].astype(np.float64) / (size - 1)
    r = np.where((x * 4).astype(int) % 2 == 0, x, 1 - y)
    g = np.sin(6.0 * np.pi * y) * 0.5 + 0.5
    b = np.where(((x * 8).astype(int) + (y * 8).astype(int)) % 2 == 0, 0.15, 0.85)
    a = np.clip(0.25 + 0.75 * x, 0, 1)
    card = np.stack([r, g, b, a], axis=-1)

            "patch_size": vcfg.patch_size, "spatial_merge_size": vcfg.spatial_merge_size,
            "temporal_patch_size": vcfg.temporal_patch_size,
            "in_channels": vcfg.in_channels,
            "num_position_embeddings": vcfg.num_position_embeddings,
            "out_hidden_size": vcfg.out_hidden_size,
            "deepstack_visual_indexes": list(vcfg.deepstack_visual_indexes),

1	"""Dump Qwen-Image-2.1's vision tower and its image-conditioned text
2	encoding, for Q8 — the oracle the Go port of an *edit's* prefix is gated
3	against.
4	
5	Everything an edit adds over a generation is on this path and nowhere else.
6	Q2 already validated the DiT's edit case (per-reference RoPE blocks, the
7	segments, the prefix cache) against `out/qi21dit` and `out/qi21block`, and
8	Q5 the VAE encoder that supplies the reference latents. What has never been
9	run in Go is the other half of a condition image: the 27-layer ViT that
10	turns its pixels into vision context, the three deepstack taps that are
11	injected into the text model's first layers, and the 3-D mrope the text
12	model uses once real image positions exist.
13	
14	So this walks all of it, stage by stage:
15	
16	  * the processor's patching — `pixel_values` is [patches, 1536] where 1536
17	    is 3 channels x 2 temporal x 16 x 16, and the temporal axis is the same
18	    frame twice. The Go side has to reproduce that layout exactly, so it is
19	    dumped rather than described;
20	  * the tower's *interpolated* position embedding. The checkpoint holds 2304
21	    = 48x48 learned positions and any image grid is a bilinear resample of
22	    them, which is four (index, weight) pairs per patch — dumped as the
23	    indices and weights the model itself computed, because reproducing the
24	    resample is the single most mistakable piece here;
25	  * the vision rotary table, every block's output, the three deepstack
26	    features (layers 8/16/24) and the 2x2 patch merger;
27	  * the text side: the 3-D mrope position ids for a sequence that contains
28	    image tokens, the input embeddings *after* the merger's output has been
29	    scattered into the `<|image_pad|>` slots, and the pipeline's own
30	    `prompt_embeds` and `image_pad_mask`.
31	
32	A fact this dump exists to pin, and the one Q8 rests on: the DiT overwrites
33	the image-slot rows with VAE latents, so vision content reaches it **only
34	through what the text tokens absorbed inside the encoder's attention**. The
35	tower conditions the text; the VAE conditions the pixels. `edit_merged_rows`
36	and `edit_prompt_embeds` are the two sides of that.
37	
38	The condition image is generated here — a deterministic 256x256 RGBA card —
39	so the dump needs no asset and two runs are byte-identical.
40	
41	    .venv/bin/python reference/dump_qi21_vision.py   (~36 GB RSS, minutes)
42	
43	The end-to-end edit oracle is a separate, heavier script: the full pipeline
44	in fp32 is ~68 GB and must run alone.
45	"""
46	
47	import json
48	import os
49	
50	import numpy as np
51	import torch
52	from diffusers import QwenImage21Pipeline
53	from PIL import Image
54	from transformers import AutoModel, Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration, Qwen3VLProcessor
55	
56	OUT = "reference/out/qi21vision"
57	MODEL = "models/Qwen-Image-2.1"
58	PROMPT = "make the sky a deep orange sunset"
59	# 256x256 is the processor's own minimum (shortest_edge is 65536 pixels), so
60	# the card passes through unresized: the grid is 16x16 patches, 64 image-pad
61	# slots, and every stage below stays small enough to read.
62	SIZE = 256
63	
64	
65	def test_card(size):
66	    """A deterministic RGBA card: colour ramps, hard edges and a gradient
67	    alpha, so the tower sees structure at every frequency it could care
68	    about. Same idea as dump_qi21_vae.py's card, at the tower's size."""
69	    y, x = np.mgrid[0:size, 0:size].astype(np.float64) / (size - 1)
70	    r = np.where((x * 4).astype(int) % 2 == 0, x, 1 - y)
71	    g = np.sin(6.0 * np.pi * y) * 0.5 + 0.5
72	    b = np.where(((x * 8).astype(int) + (y * 8).astype(int)) % 2 == 0, 0.15, 0.85)
73	    a = np.clip(0.25 + 0.75 * x, 0, 1)
74	    card = np.stack([r, g, b, a], axis=-1)
75	    return (card * 255).round().astype(np.uint8)
76	
77	
78	def main():
79	    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
80	    proc = Qwen3VLProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL, subfolder="processor")
81	    te = Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
82	        MODEL, subfolder="text_encoder", dtype=torch.float32, attn_implementation="eager"
83	    ).eval()
84	    pipe = QwenImage21Pipeline(
85	        scheduler=None, vae=None, text_encoder=te, processor=proc, transformer=None
86	    )
87	
88	    vcfg = te.config.vision_config
89	    tcfg = te.config.text_config
90	    manifest = {
91	        "template_ti2i": pipe.prompt_template_ti2i,
92	        "drop_idx": pipe._drop_idx,
93	        "image_token_id": pipe._img_token_id,
94	        "prompt": PROMPT,
95	        "size": SIZE,
96	        "vision": {
97	            "depth": vcfg.depth, "hidden_size": vcfg.hidden_size,
98	            "num_heads": vcfg.num_heads, "head_dim": vcfg.hidden_size // vcfg.num_heads,
99	            "intermediate_size": vcfg.intermediate_size, "hidden_act": vcfg.hidden_act,
100	            "patch_size": vcfg.patch_size, "spatial_merge_size": vcfg.spatial_merge_size,
101	            "temporal_patch_size": vcfg.temporal_patch_size,
102	            "in_channels": vcfg.in_channels,
103	            "num_position_embeddings": vcfg.num_position_embeddings,
104	            "out_hidden_size": vcfg.out_hidden_size,
105	            "deepstack_visual_indexes": list(vcfg.deepstack_visual_indexes),
106	        },
107	        "text": {
108	            "mrope_section": tcfg.rope_parameters.get("mrope_section"),
109	            "mrope_interleaved": tcfg.rope_parameters.get("mrope_interleaved"),
110	            "rope_theta": tcfg.rope_parameters["rope_theta"],
111	            "head_dim": tcfg.head_dim,
112	        },
113	        "tensors": {},
114	    }
115	
116	    def dump(name, t):
117	        t = t.detach().contiguous().to(torch.float32)
118	        with open(os.path.join(OUT, name + ".bin"), "wb") as fh:
119	            fh.write(t.numpy().tobytes())
120	        flat = t.flatten()
121	        manifest["tensors"][name] = {
122	            "shape": list(t.shape), "count": int(flat.numel()),
123	            "sum": float(flat.double().sum()), "absmax": float(flat.abs().max()),
124	        }
125	        print(f"  {name:26s} {str(list(t.shape)):20s} sum={flat.double().sum():+.5f} absmax={flat.abs().max():.4g}")
126	
127	    # --- the condition image, both copies -------------------------------
128	    #
129	    # The pipeline flattens alpha over white for the *vision* copy only and
130	    # feeds all four channels to the VAE. Both are dumped, because a port
131	    # that flattens once and uses it twice is a bug this pins.
132	    card = test_card(SIZE)
133	    rgba = Image.fromarray(card, mode="RGBA")
134	    white = Image.new("RGB", rgba.size, (255, 255, 255))
135	    white.paste(rgba, mask=rgba.getchannel("A"))
136	    dump("card_rgba", torch.from_numpy(card).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)
137	    dump("card_vision_rgb", torch.from_numpy(np.array(white)).permute(2, 0, 1).float()[None] / 127.5 - 1)
138	
139	    # --- what the processor produces ------------------------------------
140	    rendered = pipe.prompt_template_ti2i.format(PROMPT)
141	    inputs = proc(text=[rendered], images=[white], padding=True, padding_side="left", return_tensors="pt")
142	    ids = inputs.input_ids
143	    grid = inputs.image_grid_thw
144	    manifest["rendered"] = rendered
145	    manifest["ids"] = ids[0].tolist()
146	    manifest["grid_thw"] = grid.tolist()
147	    manifest["seq"] = int(ids.shape[1])
148	    manifest["image_pad_positions"] = [i for i, v in enumerate(ids[0].tolist()) if v == pipe._img_token_id]
149	    print(f"{ids.shape[1]} tokens, grid {grid.tolist()}, "
150	          f"{len(manifest['image_pad_positions'])} image-pad slots, drop_idx {pipe._drop_idx}")
151	    dump("pixel_values", inputs.pixel_values)
152	    dump("ids", ids.float())
153	    dump("mm_token_type_ids", inputs.mm_token_type_ids.float())
154	
155	    # --- the vision tower, stage by stage -------------------------------
156	    visual = te.model.visual
157	    caps = {}
158	    handles = [
159	        visual.patch_embed.register_forward_hook(lambda m, a, o: caps.__setitem__("patch_embed", o)),
160	        visual.pos_embed.register_forward_hook(lambda m, a, o: caps.__setitem__("pos_embed_rows", o)),
